questions.question: You imported a dataset where the 'Customer ID' column contains many repeated values. What is the most appropriate reason this column may cause issues in your report? Select the best option:

choices.A: Power BI doesn’t support text-based IDs.
choices.B: Duplicate IDs can cause incorrect aggregations or joins.
choices.C: Repeating values are only problematic for visual formatting.
choices.D: Repeating values prevent the use of column filters.

questions.explanation: Duplicate values in a primary column like Customer ID may distort aggregations and interfere with table relationships. Power BI may create ambiguous joins or misrepresent totals if unique identifiers are not maintained.

questions.question: In Power Query, you find a column that contains numeric codes representing employment statuses (e.g., 1 = Employed, 2 = Unemployed). What transformation is best practice before using this data in a report?

choices.A: Keep as-is for faster performance.
choices.B: Split the column into multiple columns.
choices.C: Replace numeric codes with descriptive text values.
choices.D: Remove the column.

questions.explanation: Replacing numeric codes with human-readable labels improves clarity, enhances filtering/slicing, and aligns with best practices for self-service BI environments.

questions.question: What Power Query feature helps you analyze the distribution and quality of values in a column before making transformations?

choices.A: M Code
choices.B: Column Statistics
choices.C: Advanced Editor
choices.D: Aggregation Panel

questions.explanation: Column Statistics, Column Quality, and Column Distribution help you understand the structure and health of your data before applying transformations. This is known as data profiling.

questions.question: You have a column called 'Address' that contains the full address as a single string (e.g., '123 Main St, New York, NY, 10001'). Which transformation is most appropriate?

choices.A: Rename the column.
choices.B: Replace commas with dashes.
choices.C: Split the column using a delimiter.
choices.D: Change data type to Date/Time.

questions.explanation: Splitting the address into individual fields (Street, City, State, Zip) improves structure and analysis capabilities. It also enables filtering or geographic mapping more efficiently.

questions.question: You want to ensure column names are descriptive and consistent across queries in Power BI. Why is this important?

choices.A: Column names affect file size.
choices.B: It reduces CPU usage during visuals.
choices.C: Descriptive names improve model readability and user experience.
choices.D: Power BI ignores column names.

questions.explanation: Clear naming conventions enhance the usability of the data model, reduce user errors, and make the model easier to understand and maintain.

questions.question: You’ve fixed all obvious data issues in Power Query, but the data types of several columns (e.g., dates, numbers) are incorrect. What might happen if you don’t fix them?

choices.A: Nothing; Power BI will auto-correct during visuals.
choices.B: Visuals may break or show incorrect aggregations.
choices.C: Power BI will convert everything to text.
choices.D: Queries will fail to load into the report.

questions.explanation: Incorrect data types can break visuals or misrepresent data. For example, sorting dates as text or aggregating text-based numbers leads to unreliable reports.

questions.question: In Power Query, which of the following tasks requires using the Advanced Editor?

choices.A: Replacing values.
choices.B: Splitting columns.
choices.C: Writing custom M transformations.
choices.D: Renaming columns.

questions.explanation: While most tasks can be performed in the UI, writing custom M transformations or applying complex logic requires editing the M code manually in the Advanced Editor.

questions.question: You want to merge two queries containing customer data. One query has basic details, the other has transaction history. What should you consider before merging?

choices.A: Both queries must use the same data type for join columns.
choices.B: One query must be marked as a fact table.
choices.C: Queries must be loaded to the model first.
choices.D: Merge is not supported in Power Query.

questions.explanation: Merge operations depend on matching values in the key columns. These columns must have the same data type, or Power Query will not match them correctly, leading to data loss or join errors.

questions.question: You’ve loaded a CSV file where the first row contains column headers, but Power BI has treated it as a data row. What should you do to correct this and why?

choices.A: Remove the first row manually
choices.B: Rename each column manually
choices.C: Use the "Use First Row as Headers" option
choices.D: Enable automatic header detection in Power BI Desktop settings

questions.explanation: Power Query assumes all rows are data unless specified. The 'Use First Row as Headers' option tells Power BI to promote the first row to headers, which is the correct approach if column names are in the first row.

questions.question: What does the “Unpivot Columns” function in Power Query Editor accomplish?

choices.A: It combines multiple queries into a single flat table
choices.B: It transposes rows into columns
choices.C: It turns selected columns into attribute-value pairs
choices.D: It aggregates values by grouping them

questions.explanation: Unpivoting transforms columns (like years) into rows, creating attribute-value pairs. This makes data easier to slice and analyze over time or categories.

questions.question: Which of the following actions does not modify the original data source when working in Power Query Editor?

choices.A: Removing columns
choices.B: Renaming tables
choices.C: Filtering rows
choices.D: All of the above

questions.explanation: Power Query only changes the view of your data inside Power BI. The original source files or databases remain unchanged regardless of transformations performed.

questions.question: You are connected to a SQL Server database. What is the most efficient way to reduce the number of columns in your dataset during the loading phase?

choices.A: Load the full table and remove columns in Power BI
choices.B: Use SQL views created by your DBA
choices.C: Use a SELECT query with specific column names
choices.D: Use DAX to hide columns after loading

questions.explanation: Using a custom SQL query with only required columns reduces data transfer and improves refresh performance by filtering at the source.

questions.question: When should you use the “Close & Apply” button in Power Query Editor?

choices.A: After loading data into Power BI for the first time
choices.B: After completing all necessary transformations
choices.C: After creating DAX measures
choices.D: Before publishing your report to the Power BI Service

questions.explanation: “Close & Apply” finalizes your transformation steps and loads the shaped data into the Power BI model, so it should be used only once data shaping is complete.

questions.question: You’ve loaded a CSV file where the first row contains column headers, but Power BI has treated it as a data row. What should you do to correct this and why?

choices.A: Remove the first row manually
choices.B: Rename each column manually
choices.C: Use the "Use First Row as Headers" option
choices.D: Enable automatic header detection in Power BI Desktop settings

questions.explanation: Power Query assumes all rows are data unless specified. The 'Use First Row as Headers' option tells Power BI to promote the first row to headers, which is the correct approach if column names are in the first row.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best reason to remove unnecessary columns early in the data transformation process?

choices.A: It visually simplifies the report view
choices.B: It reduces memory consumption and improves model performance
choices.C: It ensures that the data will refresh faster on the cloud
choices.D: It avoids SQL syntax errors in Power Query M code

questions.explanation: Early removal of columns reduces the size of the data model, which leads to better performance and faster processing in Power BI Desktop. It also makes your reports easier to manage.

questions.question: In Power Query Editor, what happens when you promote headers before removing irrelevant top rows?

choices.A: Power Query will throw an error
choices.B: The column names may be incorrect or contain actual data
choices.C: Power BI will automatically clean the top rows
choices.D: Promoting headers will delete the top row permanently

questions.explanation: If metadata or blank rows are present at the top, promoting the first row may apply incorrect column names. Always remove unnecessary top rows before using the 'Use First Row as Headers' option.

questions.question: You have a flat table with columns: ProductCategory, Subcategory, and Quantity. You want to reshape this data to show how many subcategories exist in each product category. Which feature should you use?

choices.A: Unpivot Columns
choices.B: Group By
choices.C: Pivot Columns with aggregation
choices.D: Merge Queries

questions.explanation: Pivot Columns with aggregation like 'Count' allows you to reshape the flat data into a summarized structure showing counts of subcategories per product category.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes how Power Query Editor manages transformation steps?

choices.A: Each step rewrites the original data file
choices.B: Steps are recorded and applied only once
choices.C: Steps are stored as metadata and applied at each refresh
choices.D: Steps are saved in a separate Excel file

questions.explanation: Power Query stores transformation steps in metadata and re-applies them automatically during each refresh. This ensures data remains consistent without modifying the source.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about using the right-click context menu compared to the ribbon in Power Query?

choices.A: The context menu has fewer transformation options
choices.B: The context menu is only available for numeric columns
choices.C: Both offer similar transformation options for convenience
choices.D: The ribbon must be used for advanced transformations

questions.explanation: Both the ribbon and the right-click menu offer similar tools like renaming, unpivoting, and removing columns. The context menu provides quick access to commonly used transformations.

questions.question: What is the impact of changing the order of applied steps in the Power Query Editor?

choices.A: It has no effect on the final dataset
choices.B: It might cause transformation errors or incorrect data output
choices.C: It speeds up the refresh rate of the data source
choices.D: It disables column-level security features

questions.explanation: Changing the order of transformation steps can lead to incorrect results or errors. For example, if a column is renamed after it's removed, it will cause a step failure.

questions.question: When should you use the 'Close & Apply' button in Power Query Editor?

choices.A: After loading data into Power BI for the first time
choices.B: After completing all necessary transformations
choices.C: After creating DAX measures
choices.D: Before publishing your report to the Power BI Service

questions.explanation: 'Close & Apply' finalizes your transformations in Power Query and loads the data into the model. It should only be used after shaping is complete.

questions.question: You are reviewing query names in Power BI and find one named 'vSalesData2024'. What is the most appropriate action to simplify this name?

choices.A: Keep the name as it is to preserve the source naming convention.
choices.B: Change it to 'Sales' to make it shorter.
choices.C: Rename it to 'Sales Data 2024' to improve clarity.
choices.D: Replace it with 'FactSales' to follow a technical naming style.

questions.explanation: Simplifying data structure aims for clear, meaningful, and user-friendly names. The prefix 'v' (view) can confuse users. Adding the year improves distinction between similar queries. 'Sales Data 2024' is descriptive and avoids unnecessary technical jargon.

questions.question: Why is it recommended to replace null values with zero in numerical columns such as freight costs?

choices.A: To avoid loading errors during data refresh.
choices.B: To match SQL query outputs.
choices.C: To ensure correct aggregate calculations like averages.
choices.D: To prevent column type mismatch errors.

questions.explanation: Null values are excluded from aggregates like averages, which can lead to misleading metrics. Replacing nulls with zero ensures values are included properly, improving calculation accuracy.

questions.question: Which of the following actions CANNOT be performed directly in Power Query Editor?

choices.A: Replacing a value in a column.
choices.B: Renaming a table (query).
choices.C: Editing a single cell value manually.
choices.D: Removing duplicate rows from a column.

questions.explanation: Power Query Editor does not allow manual editing of individual cells. Instead, transformations are applied through functions like Replace Values, which ensures repeatable, automated data shaping.

questions.question: After removing duplicates from the 'Category Name' column, what is a best practice if you also want to retain the original table?

choices.A: Use the 'Group By' feature.
choices.B: Copy the table before removing duplicates.
choices.C: Create a relationship between the column and itself.
choices.D: Export the table to Excel for backup.

questions.explanation: Duplicating the table before removing duplicates keeps both the original data and a clean unique-values table, which is useful for creating dimension tables in a star schema.

questions.question: Which naming practice is LEAST recommended when renaming columns or tables in Power BI?

choices.A: Replacing underscores with spaces.
choices.B: Using descriptive business terms.
choices.C: Using commonly understood acronyms.
choices.D: Applying very short abbreviations to save space.

questions.explanation: Very short or cryptic abbreviations can confuse users. Clarity and consistency are more important for usability than saving space.

questions.question: You replaced a value in a column using the Replace Values feature, but the change didn’t apply to all rows. What is the MOST likely reason?

choices.A: The column type was numeric, and Replace Values works only on text.
choices.B: The value had a different case or extra spaces.
choices.C: Replace Values only affects the first 1000 rows.
choices.D: You forgot to press 'Enter' after typing the value.

questions.explanation: Replace Values is case-sensitive and sensitive to extra spaces. Mismatched cases or spaces cause the replacement to fail on some rows.

questions.question: Which of the following would best improve semantic clarity in your Power BI data model?

choices.A: Adding technical prefixes like 'tbl_' or 'dim_' to all tables.
choices.B: Keeping column names consistent with SQL table names.
choices.C: Replacing underscores and abbreviations with readable names.
choices.D: Using upper-case letters to highlight important fields.

questions.explanation: Power BI reports target business users, so clear, readable names without technical prefixes or underscores improve understanding and usability.

questions.question: After making several transformations in Power Query Editor, what must you do to ensure your changes are applied to the Power BI data model?

choices.A: Close Power Query Editor without saving.
choices.B: Click Close & Apply to save and load changes.
choices.C: Press Refresh in Power BI Desktop.
choices.D: Export the query to Excel and re-import it.

questions.explanation: Changes in Power Query Editor only affect the data model when you click Close & Apply. This commits and loads transformed data for reporting.

questions.question: Where can you review the list of transformation steps you have applied to a query in Power Query Editor?

choices.A: In the Applied Steps section of the Query Settings pane.
choices.B: In the Data view of Power BI Desktop.
choices.C: In the Relationships pane.
choices.D: In the Power BI Service online portal.

questions.explanation: The Applied Steps list in the Query Settings pane documents every transformation applied, enabling review, editing, or deletion.

questions.question: Why is it important to consider the length and format of values when replacing or naming them for reports?

choices.A: Long values improve data accuracy and detail.
choices.B: Values that are too long may not fit on visuals and can reduce readability.
choices.C: Short values are always better regardless of meaning.
choices.D: Acronyms are preferred to save space on reports.

questions.explanation: Values that are too long can clutter or truncate visuals, making reports hard to read. It’s important to balance clarity with length for optimal readability.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended practice when renaming values in Power Query for reports?

choices.A: Using consistent abbreviations agreed upon in the organization.
choices.B: Replacing underscores ('_') with spaces in values.
choices.C: Using acronyms frequently to save space.
choices.D: Choosing values that make sense in report context.

questions.explanation: Frequent use of acronyms can confuse report consumers unless the acronyms are well understood; clarity is preferred.

questions.question: If you realize that a transformation step applied early in the Power Query steps causes an error in subsequent steps, what is the best course of action?

choices.A: Delete all steps and start over.
choices.B: Use the Applied Steps pane to find and modify or remove the problematic step.
choices.C: Ignore the error and continue editing other queries.
choices.D: Close Power Query without applying changes.

questions.explanation: The Applied Steps pane allows you to identify and fix or remove problematic steps, which resolves errors without redoing the entire query.

questions.question: What is the primary reason you should evaluate and change data types in Power Query Editor before loading data into Power BI?

choices.A: It improves the visual formatting of charts and tables
choices.B: It avoids the need to use DAX expressions
choices.C: It ensures correct calculations, relationships, and hierarchies
choices.D: It saves memory by reducing file size

questions.explanation: Incorrect data types can break time-based DAX functions, prevent relationships between tables, and stop Power BI from generating hierarchies like Year → Month → Day. Reviewing data types early in Power Query avoids these critical issues.

questions.question: You import a CSV file containing an 'OrderDate' column. Power BI sets its data type to Text. What issue are you most likely to encounter if you don’t correct this?

choices.A: The column won’t be visible in visuals
choices.B: DAX measures using time intelligence functions will fail
choices.C: You won’t be able to rename the column
choices.D: The file will not load into Power BI

questions.explanation: Time intelligence functions like TOTALYTD() require a proper Date data type. If 'OrderDate' is set as Text, these functions return errors because they cannot interpret the values as dates.

questions.question: Which of the following actions in Power Query Editor will save a data type change as a step in the applied steps pane?

choices.A: Changing the column name
choices.B: Selecting the correct data type from the icon next to the column name
choices.C: Filtering a column to remove blanks
choices.D: Creating a measure in the report view

questions.explanation: Changing the data type using the icon next to the column name in Power Query creates a “Changed Type” step. All transformation steps are recorded and reapplied each time the data is refreshed.

questions.question: Which data sources are most likely to cause data type detection errors in Power BI?

choices.A: SQL Server databases
choices.B: Azure Synapse Analytics
choices.C: CSV and Excel files
choices.D: SharePoint lists

questions.explanation: Flat files like CSV and Excel are more error-prone because data entry is manual and doesn’t enforce strict typing like databases do. Mistakes such as typing text in a numeric column can lead to incorrect type detection.

questions.question: In the Report view, a column containing dates shows only as a flat list and doesn’t allow a Year/Month/Day breakdown. What is the likely cause?

choices.A: Auto date/time is turned off
choices.B: Column has null values
choices.C: Column is set as text instead of date
choices.D: The column is hidden in the data model

questions.explanation: Hierarchies are only available if the column is correctly set as a Date. If it is set as Text, Power BI cannot generate the automatic hierarchy (even if auto date/time is enabled).

questions.question: What happens when you change the data type of a column in Power Query Editor?

choices.A: The change is permanent and stored in the source file
choices.B: A new transformation step (Changed Type) is created and applied at every data refresh
choices.C: The data type is changed only for the current report session and resets after refresh
choices.D: Power BI automatically creates a new table with corrected data types

questions.explanation: Power Query saves all transformations as steps. Changing a column’s data type creates a "Changed Type" step that is reapplied each time data refreshes, ensuring data consistency without altering the original source.

questions.question: Why is it considered a best practice to disable Auto Date/Time and use a dedicated Date table in Power BI?

choices.A: To speed up data import from Excel files
choices.B: To prevent Power BI from generating automatic hierarchies and improve performance
choices.C: To automatically correct wrong data types in date columns
choices.D: To reduce the size of the Power BI file by removing unused dates

questions.explanation: Using a dedicated Date table gives you full control over date hierarchies and improves performance. Auto Date/Time creates hidden date tables that can bloat the model and cause confusion.

questions.question: If a column contains numeric values but is detected as Text, what is a likely impact?

choices.A: You cannot apply filters to that column
choices.B: Power BI will ignore that column during data refresh
choices.C: Aggregations like SUM or AVERAGE will fail or produce incorrect results
choices.D: The column will not appear in the Fields pane

questions.explanation: Numerical operations require numeric data types. If a column is text, SUM or AVERAGE won’t work correctly because the data isn’t recognized as numeric.

questions.question: Where in Power BI Desktop can you change the data type of a column after data has been loaded?

choices.A: Power Query Editor only
choices.B: Report view via the Column Tools ribbon
choices.C: Modeling tab only
choices.D: Data source settings

questions.explanation: While it’s best to change data types in Power Query, you can change them later in the Report view using the Column Tools ribbon. However, this affects only the loaded data model, not the query steps.

questions.question: What problem arises if you don't correct a date column data type and attempt to create a relationship with another table’s date field?

choices.A: Relationship will be automatically corrected by Power BI
choices.B: The relationship will fail because data types must match
choices.C: The relationship will be created but will produce incorrect results
choices.D: You can create the relationship but cannot use it in visuals

questions.explanation: Power BI requires columns involved in relationships to have compatible data types. If one column is Text and the other is Date, the relationship cannot be established.

questions.question: You are preparing to append three tables: Employees, Customers, and Suppliers. However, only the Customers table contains the column named PhoneNumber. The other two have a column called ContactNumber. What must be done before appending?

choices.A: Append the tables as they are; Power BI automatically matches columns with similar data types
choices.B: Rename PhoneNumber to ContactNumber in Customers
choices.C: Rename all ContactNumber columns to PhoneNumber in all three tables
choices.D: Merge the tables instead of appending them

questions.explanation: When appending queries, column names must exactly match across tables. If they differ, Power BI treats them as separate columns. Renaming all ContactNumber columns to PhoneNumber ensures a single combined column in the appended table.

questions.question: You want to merge two tables: Orders and OrderDetails. Orders has 500 rows, and OrderDetails has 2000 rows. If you use an Inner Join on OrderID, which result is correct?

choices.A: The resulting table will have 2500 rows
choices.B: The resulting table will contain only rows where OrderID exists in both tables
choices.C: The resulting table will have all 500 rows from Orders, regardless of matches
choices.D: You cannot perform this merge unless both tables have exactly the same number of rows

questions.explanation: An Inner Join returns only rows that have matching keys in both tables. Non-matching rows are excluded, so the result includes only OrderIDs present in both Orders and OrderDetails.

questions.question: In Power Query, which of the following steps is NOT required before appending three data tables for a unified contact list?

choices.A: Removing unnecessary columns
choices.B: Sorting all tables by the same column
choices.C: Standardizing column headers
choices.D: Ensuring data types match for each column

questions.explanation: Sorting rows is not necessary when appending because append stacks rows vertically. However, columns must be standardized in name and data type, and irrelevant columns removed.

questions.question: You’ve appended Customers, Suppliers, and Employees into a master table using “Append Queries as New.” What is the main advantage of using "Append Queries as New" instead of "Append Queries"?

choices.A: It creates a reference table that updates only when manually refreshed
choices.B: It creates a brand new table, preserving the original tables untouched
choices.C: It automatically merges columns with similar names
choices.D: It removes the need to transform individual tables before combining them

questions.explanation: "Append Queries as New" creates a new query/table without modifying the original tables, which helps preserve source data and allows building transformations on a fresh combined dataset.

questions.question: When merging two tables in Power Query, what happens if the column used as the join key contains null values?

choices.A: Nulls are automatically matched together
choices.B: Rows with null in the key column are excluded from the merge
choices.C: The merge will fail unless nulls are replaced first
choices.D: All rows with nulls are matched by default and included

questions.explanation: Null values in the join key do not match any other value, including other nulls, so rows with null keys are excluded from the merged result.

questions.question: What will happen if you append two tables with the same column headers but different data types for one column, e.g., ID is text in one table and numeric in another?

choices.A: Power BI automatically converts data types to match
choices.B: The append operation fails with an error
choices.C: Power BI converts all values to text or the broader data type
choices.D: The column with conflicting types will be split into two separate columns in the appended table

questions.explanation: Power BI promotes data types to the broader or more flexible type to unify the column during append. For example, numeric data may be converted to text to avoid conflicts.

questions.question: Which of the following join types will result in a merged table that includes all rows from both tables, showing nulls where no match exists?

choices.A: Left Outer
choices.B: Right Outer
choices.C: Inner
choices.D: Full Outer

questions.explanation: A Full Outer Join includes all rows from both tables. For rows without matching keys in the other table, columns are filled with nulls.

questions.question: You want to create a merged table from two tables with columns: EmployeeID in the first and EmpID in the second, representing the same data. What is the best way to proceed?

choices.A: Merge directly using these columns as they have different names but same data
choices.B: Rename one column to match the other before merging
choices.C: Use append instead of merge
choices.D: Create a new calculated column combining the two before merging

questions.explanation: Merge operations require selecting matching columns by name in each table. Renaming columns to the same name ensures the join uses the correct keys.

questions.question: In which scenario would you prefer merging tables over appending them?

choices.A: When you want to stack multiple datasets vertically
choices.B: When you want to add related data from a lookup table as new columns
choices.C: When all tables have the same structure
choices.D: When you want to create a new query without modifying original data

questions.explanation: Merging adds columns from one table to another based on keys (like lookups). Appending stacks rows vertically and is not appropriate for adding related columns.

questions.question: You have a large semantic model with many tables. Which is a valid reason to combine tables via append?

choices.A: To reduce the number of tables and simplify report building
choices.B: To create relationships between tables
choices.C: To normalize the data model
choices.D: To add calculated columns across tables

questions.explanation: Appending reduces the number of tables by consolidating those with similar roles, simplifying the model and navigation. Relationships and normalization are separate design considerations.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains the purpose of data profiling in Power BI?

choices.A: Creating relationships between tables
choices.B: Designing complex visuals on the report canvas
choices.C: Studying data structure, anomalies, and statistical patterns
choices.D: Configuring row-level security in the model

questions.explanation: Data profiling focuses on understanding the structure, quality, and distribution of data before building visuals. This involves identifying anomalies, analyzing column statistics, and verifying data consistency. Options A, B, and D relate to other aspects of Power BI but not specifically to profiling.

questions.question: By default, Power BI performs column profiling on which portion of the data?

choices.A: The entire dataset
choices.B: The first 10,000 rows
choices.C: The first 1,000 rows
choices.D: A random 5% sample of rows

questions.explanation: Power Query Editor profiles the first 1,000 rows by default to balance performance and insight. This can be changed to profile the entire dataset if needed.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is TRUE about 'distinct' and 'unique' values in Column Distribution?

choices.A: Distinct values exclude nulls, while unique values include them
choices.B: Distinct counts all different values including nulls and duplicates; unique counts values appearing once without nulls
choices.C: Unique values include all repeated entries
choices.D: Power BI does not differentiate between distinct and unique in profiling

questions.explanation: Distinct values include all different values, including duplicates and nulls. Unique values only count those that appear once and exclude duplicates and nulls. This distinction helps identify data repetition or uniqueness.

questions.question: Which metric is NOT provided by the Column Quality feature?

choices.A: Percentage of valid values
choices.B: Count of duplicate entries
choices.C: Percentage of error values
choices.D: Percentage of empty values

questions.explanation: Column Quality shows percentages of valid, error, and empty values. The count of duplicate entries is shown in Column Distribution, not Column Quality.

questions.question: Which of the following insights can Power BI provide for numeric columns via Column Profile?

choices.A: Number of even and odd values
choices.B: Total number of charts created using that column
choices.C: Data types used in the entire dataset
choices.D: Currency symbols detected in numeric values

questions.explanation: For numeric columns, Power BI shows counts of even and odd values, min, max, average, standard deviation, null and zero counts. The other options are unrelated to profiling.

questions.question: How can the Value Distribution feature help detect bad data?

choices.A: It filters columns with NULLs
choices.B: It visualizes each unique value and how often it appears
choices.C: It highlights all columns that contain currency symbols
choices.D: It shows percentage of column transformations

questions.explanation: Value Distribution shows a bar chart of unique values and their frequency. This helps detect overrepresented or underrepresented values and possible data quality issues.

questions.question: What real-life issue can profiling help detect before building visuals?

choices.A: Incorrect DAX formulas
choices.B: Data model relationships missing
choices.C: Visual formatting errors
choices.D: Inconsistent or outdated data entries

questions.explanation: Profiling helps identify inconsistent or outdated data, anomalies, or errors early. Other options relate to later stages of report development.

questions.question: Which action applies the transformations made during data profiling back to the Power BI model?

choices.A: Save as Template
choices.B: Apply Data Snapshot
choices.C: Refresh Now
choices.D: Close & Apply

questions.explanation: Close & Apply applies the changes made in Power Query Editor and loads the cleaned data into Power BI Desktop.

questions.question: Where in Power BI Desktop can you view and edit the underlying data structures before profiling?

choices.A: Data view
choices.B: Report view
choices.C: Model tab
choices.D: Power Query Editor only

questions.explanation: The Model tab lets you view and edit the semantic data model, including table and column properties and relationships, before profiling the data.

questions.question: What feature allows you to create, edit, or delete relationships between tables in Power BI Desktop?

choices.A: Manage Relationships on the ribbon
choices.B: Column Distribution pane
choices.C: Column Profile view
choices.D: Data Refresh settings

questions.explanation: Manage Relationships on the Model tab ribbon enables you to create, edit, or delete relationships between tables.

questions.question: In text columns, what do the minimum and maximum values represent in Power Query’s profiling?

choices.A: Length of the shortest and longest text strings
choices.B: The first and last values alphabetically
choices.C: The earliest and latest dates in the column
choices.D: The smallest and largest numerical values in the text

questions.explanation: For text columns, the minimum and maximum represent the first and last values alphabetically, not string length or dates.

questions.question: Why might you choose to profile only the first 1,000 rows rather than the entire dataset?

choices.A: To improve performance and speed
choices.B: Because Power BI does not support profiling entire datasets
choices.C: Because the first 1,000 rows are always representative
choices.D: To apply security rules faster

questions.explanation: Profiling the entire dataset can be slow; profiling the first 1,000 rows improves performance while still providing useful insights.

questions.question: Which metric(s) in Power Query help identify outliers in numeric data?

choices.A: Distinct and unique counts
choices.B: Min and Max values, standard deviation
choices.C: Percentage of empty values
choices.D: Number of tables in the model

questions.explanation: Min, max, and standard deviation metrics help identify numeric outliers by showing values that are unusually high or low compared to the rest.

questions.question: After profiling and editing data in Power Query Editor, what should you do next to use this data in report visuals?

choices.A: Export data as CSV
choices.B: Close Power Query without saving
choices.C: Select Close & Apply to load changes
choices.D: Refresh the data model without applying changes

questions.explanation: Close & Apply saves and applies all changes from Power Query Editor back to Power BI Desktop, making the data ready for reporting.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of profiling data before building reports?

choices.A: Ensuring data is complete and clean
choices.B: Discovering the distribution of values
choices.C: Automatically building visuals without manual intervention
choices.D: Identifying anomalies and errors early

questions.explanation: Profiling helps you understand and prepare your data; it does not automatically generate report visuals.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about M code in Power Query is TRUE?

choices.A: M code is executed bottom-up, with each step referencing the next one.
choices.B: The `in` keyword must always appear at the beginning of the M script.
choices.C: Reordering steps in M code can break the query logic.
choices.D: Each M code step can reference any other step, regardless of position.

questions.explanation:
M code is executed top-down, meaning each step can only refer to previously defined steps. Changing the order of steps may break dependencies, causing errors. 

- A is incorrect because execution is top-down.
- B is incorrect because the 'in' keyword appears near the end.
- D is incorrect because future steps cannot be referenced.

questions.question: When modifying M code directly in the Advanced Editor, what should you always consider?

choices.A: Renaming a step variable in the middle of the script has no effect.
choices.B: Changing the database name in a connection string is not possible in M.
choices.C: Every step name (before `=`) must be unique and valid.
choices.D: Comments are not allowed in M code.

questions.explanation: Each step name is a variable and must be unique and syntactically valid. Renaming a step affects all references. You can change database names in M code. M supports comments using '//'.

questions.question:
Given the following M code, what is the name of the final output step?

let
    Source = Excel.Workbook(File.Contents("sales.xlsx")),
    Filtered = Table.SelectRows(Source, each [Region] = "West"),
    Cleaned = Table.RemoveColumns(Filtered,{"UnnecessaryColumn"})
in
    Cleaned

choices.A: Source
choices.B: Filtered
choices.C: Cleaned
choices.D: sales.xlsx

questions.explanation: The final output is the value specified after the 'in' keyword, which here is 'Cleaned'.

questions.question: You moved a data type transformation step before the column it refers to was added. What will most likely happen?

choices.A: The data will refresh normally.
choices.B: Power BI will automatically adjust the step order.
choices.C: You will get a 'column not found' error.
choices.D: M will ignore the mistake and continue processing.

questions.explanation: Because M code steps are dependent on previous steps, attempting to transform a non-existent column will result in an error. Power BI does not automatically reorder steps.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid reason to use the Advanced Editor in Power Query?

choices.A: To write DAX expressions for calculated columns.
choices.B: To customize transformations beyond what the GUI offers.
choices.C: To import visuals into Power BI reports.
choices.D: To directly manipulate data model relationships.

questions.explanation: The Advanced Editor allows you to view and edit the M code behind Power Query steps, enabling custom transformations beyond the graphical interface. DAX, visuals, and relationships are handled elsewhere.

questions.question: When you perform data shaping actions in Power Query’s GUI, what happens behind the scenes?

choices.A: No code is created unless you manually write M code.
choices.B: Power Query automatically generates M code for each transformation step.
choices.C: Each step creates a DAX formula instead of M code.
choices.D: The Advanced Editor stays empty until you type something manually.

questions.explanation: Each action in the GUI creates corresponding M code automatically, visible in the Advanced Editor. You do not need to write M code manually for transformations.

questions.question: Which of these is a valid way to experiment safely in the Advanced Editor?

choices.A: Delete all the existing steps and start from scratch without saving.
choices.B: Modify one step at a time and check if the query still works before continuing.
choices.C: Change the order of all steps randomly to see the results.
choices.D: Remove the `in` statement to speed up execution.

questions.explanation: Safe experimentation involves small incremental changes and validating results after each modification. Deleting or randomly reordering steps risks breaking the query. The 'in' statement is mandatory.

questions.question: If you rename a step variable in the Advanced Editor, what must you ensure?

choices.A: You also rename all references to that variable in subsequent steps.
choices.B: The variable name can be the same as any other step for convenience.
choices.C: Renaming a step variable doesn’t affect any other part of the code.
choices.D: You only need to change the name in the last step.

questions.explanation: Later steps reference previous steps by their variable names. Renaming a step requires updating all references, otherwise the query breaks.

questions.question: What is a key advantage of editing queries in the Advanced Editor compared to using the GUI?

choices.A: You can modify the underlying M code to implement transformations not possible via GUI.
choices.B: It automatically optimizes query performance better than GUI.
choices.C: The GUI does not allow adding any steps to the query.
choices.D: You cannot view the query steps in the GUI once edited in the Advanced Editor.

questions.explanation: Advanced Editor gives full access to M language, allowing custom transformations beyond GUI capabilities. The GUI still shows steps after editing.

questions.question: What happens if you omit or incorrectly specify the `in` statement in your M code?

choices.A: The query returns all steps as output.
choices.B: Power Query throws an error or returns no output.
choices.C: The query ignores the missing `in` statement and returns the first step.
choices.D: The last step automatically becomes the output.

questions.explanation: The `in` statement specifies the final output of the query. Omitting or miswriting it causes an error or blank result.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of using an Import model in Power BI?

choices.A: Supports all data source types including files, databases, and web pages
choices.B: Data is cached in memory for optimized query performance
choices.C: Allows for direct querying of live data without storing it in memory
choices.D: Supports calculated tables created with DAX

questions.explanation: Import models load data into memory and cache it for fast analytic queries. Direct querying of live data without importing is the behavior of DirectQuery mode, not Import mode.

questions.question: What is the maximum dataset size for an Import model when published on a shared capacity workspace in Power BI?

choices.A: 10 GB
choices.B: 1 GB (compressed model size)
choices.C: No limit
choices.D: 500 MB

questions.explanation: On shared capacity, Power BI imposes a strict limit of 1 GB per dataset, based on the compressed size of the model in memory. Exceeding this limit will cause refresh failures.

questions.question: Which data reduction technique is NOT recommended to optimize an Import model size?

choices.A: Removing unnecessary columns
choices.B: Using calculated columns in the model instead of custom columns in Power Query
choices.C: Grouping and summarizing fact tables
choices.D: Optimizing column data types with numeric preference

questions.explanation: It is preferable to use custom columns in Power Query rather than calculated columns within the model to reduce model size and refresh time. Calculated columns in the model increase memory usage.

questions.question: How often can you schedule data refresh for an Import model on a Power BI Premium (dedicated) capacity?

choices.A: 8 times per day
choices.B: 48 times per day
choices.C: Unlimited refreshes per day
choices.D: Only once per day

questions.explanation: On dedicated (Premium) capacity, Power BI allows up to 48 scheduled refreshes per day to keep the imported data current. This is significantly higher than the 8 refreshes per day on shared capacity.

questions.question: What is the purpose of incremental refresh in Power BI Import models?

choices.A: To import data from multiple sources simultaneously
choices.B: To refresh only updated partitions instead of the whole table
choices.C: To automatically convert Import models to DirectQuery
choices.D: To disable scheduled refresh

questions.explanation: Incremental refresh allows the dataset to refresh only partitions of data that have changed, reducing refresh time and resource consumption. It avoids reloading the entire table, which can be costly for large fact tables.

questions.question: Which scenario would suggest considering DirectQuery or hybrid tables instead of an Import model?

choices.A: When model size is less than 1 GB
choices.B: When scheduled refresh frequency of 8 times/day is sufficient
choices.C: When near real-time data updates are required and refresh latency is not acceptable
choices.D: When using only static data sources

questions.explanation: If your data needs to be updated more frequently than the scheduled refresh limits or with minimal latency, DirectQuery or hybrid tables are better suited as they support near real-time querying without needing full dataset refreshes.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Power BI dataset size refers to the compressed size of the model?

choices.A: It measures the raw volume of data collected from the source system
choices.B: It is unrelated to how much memory Power BI consumes
choices.C: It affects the dataset refresh limits on Power BI service
choices.D: It only applies to DirectQuery models

questions.explanation: The 1 GB limit refers to the compressed size of the Power BI model in memory, not the raw size of the source data. This compressed size directly affects the ability to refresh datasets on the Power BI service.

questions.question: What is the default storage mode used by Power BI Desktop when loading data with "Get data"?

choices.A: DirectQuery
choices.B: Import
choices.C: Composite model
choices.D: Live Connection

questions.explanation: By default, Power BI Desktop uses Import storage mode, meaning data is imported and cached in memory for best performance and full functionality.

questions.question: Which Power BI feature allows advanced users to automate partition creation and management for large Import models?

choices.A: DirectQuery setup wizard
choices.B: XMLA endpoint with scripting capabilities
choices.C: Power Query Editor
choices.D: Auto date/time setting

questions.explanation: The XMLA endpoint available in Power BI Premium allows advanced data modelers to customize partitioning strategies and automate partition management via scripts, improving large dataset refresh and management.

questions.question: What happens during a default table refresh in an Import model?

choices.A: Only new rows are added
choices.B: Power BI merges new data with existing data
choices.C: All data in the table is removed and reloaded completely
choices.D: No data is refreshed unless incremental refresh is enabled

questions.explanation: By default, Power BI removes all data from the table and reloads it completely during a refresh, which can be resource-intensive and slow, especially for large tables.

questions.question: Which Power BI feature can you disable to reduce unnecessary data storage and improve model refresh performance in Import models?

choices.A: Auto date/time
choices.B: Incremental refresh
choices.C: Calculated tables
choices.D: DirectQuery storage mode

questions.explanation: Auto date/time creates hidden date tables automatically, which can increase model size unnecessarily. Disabling it reduces data load and improves refresh times.

questions.question: In Import models, why might you disable the “Enable load” option in Power Query queries?

choices.A: To prevent the query from being visible in the report
choices.B: To avoid loading intermediate or staging queries into the model, saving memory
choices.C: To automatically refresh the query more frequently
choices.D: To convert the query to DirectQuery mode

questions.explanation: Disabling query load for intermediate queries avoids loading them into the model, which saves memory and reduces dataset size without affecting the refresh of dependent queries.

questions.question: What is a key capability of calculated tables in an Import model?

choices.A: They can only be created in DirectQuery mode
choices.B: They enable defining tables using DAX formulas for advanced data modeling
choices.C: They automatically refresh independently of the model refresh schedule
choices.D: They store data outside of the Power BI dataset

questions.explanation: Calculated tables are created within the model using DAX formulas, allowing for advanced data transformations and modeling inside the Import model.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about source groups in Power BI models is TRUE?

choices.A: A model can have multiple import source groups but only one DirectQuery source group.
choices.B: A DirectQuery model can only have one source group, which contains all DirectQuery tables.
choices.C: Composite models consist of a single source group.
choices.D: Calculated tables are always stored in a DirectQuery source group.

questions.explanation: In Power BI, a DirectQuery model includes tables with storage mode set to DirectQuery and belongs to a single source group. Import and DirectQuery models each comprise only one source group. Composite models contain more than one source group. Therefore, option B is correct.

questions.question: What is the primary reason to use a DirectQuery model instead of importing data in Power BI?

choices.A: To allow use of all Power Query transformations.
choices.B: To enable importing large data warehouses efficiently.
choices.C: To handle large or fast-changing data sources without data refresh.
choices.D: To increase report query speed in all scenarios.

questions.explanation: DirectQuery is ideal for large or frequently changing data sources because it queries data in real-time without requiring data refresh. Importing large datasets is impractical and some Power Query transformations are not supported in DirectQuery mode.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of using DirectQuery?

choices.A: Enforcing source-level Row-Level Security (RLS) without replicating rules in Power BI.
choices.B: Connecting to on-premises data sources when data cannot leave the premises.
choices.C: Supporting all Power Query M transformations without restrictions.
choices.D: Allowing chaining of up to three models for personalization or extension.

questions.explanation: DirectQuery does not support all Power Query transformations because queries must translate into native queries understood by the source system. Therefore, option C is false.

questions.question: Which scenario best describes when to enforce RLS through the source database in a DirectQuery model?

choices.A: When the source database supports RLS and single sign-on is configured.
choices.B: When Power BI can easily replicate RLS rules within the model.
choices.C: When the source database is a non-relational data source.
choices.D: When the model contains only import mode tables.

questions.explanation: Enforcing RLS at the source database requires that the database supports RLS and that single sign-on (SSO) is configured. This avoids replicating security rules in Power BI.

questions.question: Why might analytic query performance be slow when using DirectQuery?

choices.A: Because all Power Query transformations are done locally before sending queries.
choices.B: Due to lack of database optimization like indexes or materialized views.
choices.C: Because DirectQuery caches all data in Power BI, causing delays.
choices.D: Because DirectQuery doesn’t send queries to the source system.

questions.explanation: Query performance depends on the optimization of the source database. Without indexes or materialized views, analytic queries may be slow. DirectQuery sends queries live to the source and does not cache all data locally.

questions.question: What happens when you add new import or DirectQuery tables to a Power BI dataset converted from a remote DirectQuery dataset?

choices.A: The model remains a simple DirectQuery model with one source group.
choices.B: The model becomes a composite model with multiple source groups.
choices.C: The original dataset loses all connection to the remote model.
choices.D: Power BI disables the DirectQuery functionality.

questions.explanation: Adding new tables with different storage modes creates new source groups, turning the model into a composite model which supports multiple source groups.

questions.question: What is the role of user-defined aggregation tables in a DirectQuery model?

choices.A: They allow Power BI users to directly see and interact with these tables in reports.
choices.B: They improve performance by satisfying higher-grain queries and can query materialized views.
choices.C: They replace the need for source database optimizations like indexes.
choices.D: They disable row-level security for faster analytics.

questions.explanation: User-defined aggregation tables are hidden from users and calculations, designed to improve query performance by using higher-level aggregations and possibly querying materialized views.

questions.question: Which of these is TRUE regarding the chaining of Power BI datasets in DirectQuery mode?

choices.A: You can chain up to five models, allowing unlimited extensions.
choices.B: Chained models cannot add new measures or calculated columns.
choices.C: Chaining enables creating local models that extend or personalize remote datasets.
choices.D: Chaining is only available for import mode datasets.

questions.explanation: Power BI supports chaining up to three models in DirectQuery mode, allowing local models to extend or personalize remote datasets by adding measures or calculated columns.

questions.question: In a Power BI model, how many import source groups and DirectQuery source groups can coexist without creating a composite model?

choices.A: Multiple import and multiple DirectQuery source groups.
choices.B: One import source group and one DirectQuery source group.
choices.C: One import source group only.
choices.D: Multiple import source groups but only one DirectQuery source group.

questions.explanation: A model with more than one source group is considered a composite model. A non-composite model contains either a single import source group or a single DirectQuery source group.

questions.question: Which Power Query (M) transformations are typically NOT supported in DirectQuery mode, and why?

choices.A: Simple filters and column renaming, because they cannot be translated.
choices.B: Pivot and unpivot transformations, because they cannot be translated to native queries.
choices.C: Adding calculated columns, because Power BI does not allow calculations in DirectQuery.
choices.D: None, all transformations are supported equally.

questions.explanation: Certain transformations like pivot and unpivot cannot be translated into native queries required by DirectQuery, hence they are not supported.

questions.question: How can analytic queries on a DirectQuery model impact the source system?

choices.A: They have no impact because queries run only on cached data.
choices.B: They can reduce performance for OLTP workloads due to additional query load.
choices.C: They improve source system performance by optimizing queries.
choices.D: They isolate the analytic workload from transactional systems automatically.

questions.explanation: Because DirectQuery sends live queries to the source, the additional workload can degrade the performance of transactional systems (OLTP).

questions.question: Why is collaboration with the database owner recommended when developing a DirectQuery model?

choices.A: Because the database owner controls Power BI licensing.
choices.B: To ensure the database is optimized and can handle the additional workload.
choices.C: Because the database owner must write all DAX measures.
choices.D: It is not necessary; Power BI handles everything automatically.

questions.explanation: Collaborating with the database owner is important to optimize the database (indexes, materialized views, resources) so it can support the analytic workload generated by DirectQuery.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the role of DAX in Power BI?

choices.A: A query language used exclusively for paginated reports
choices.B: The language used for creating calculated columns and measures in Power BI models
choices.C: The query language used to connect Power BI directly to external databases
choices.D: A language used only in Excel's Analyze in Excel feature

questions.explanation: DAX (Data Analysis Expressions) is the primary language used within Power BI to create calculated columns, measures, and expressions. It allows you to define custom calculations that extend the model’s analytical capabilities. Although MDX is also used (especially for paginated reports and Analyze in Excel), DAX is the standard for Power BI Desktop modeling and reporting.

questions.question: What is a Power BI dataset?

choices.A: A live connection to an external database without any data imported
choices.B: A published Power BI model acting as a data source for reports and dashboards
choices.C: A raw data file imported into Power BI Desktop
choices.D: A set of Excel tables linked directly to Power BI

questions.explanation: A Power BI dataset refers to the model published to the Power BI Service after development in Power BI Desktop. It acts as the source of data for reports and dashboards. Not all datasets are imported data; some represent live connections or streaming data, but the key point is that the dataset is a published artifact in the Power BI environment.

questions.question: During the execution of an analytic query in Power BI, which phase involves dividing the query results into groups where filter values are visible in the output?

choices.A: Filter (Slicing)
choices.B: Summarize
choices.C: Group (Dicing)
choices.D: Import

questions.explanation: The Group phase (also called dicing) divides the query results into visible groups, and the filter values used for grouping appear in the output (e.g., sales by customer or quarter). The Filter phase narrows data but the filter values are not visible in the result; Summarize produces aggregated values; Import is a storage mode and unrelated to query phases.

questions.question: What is the main characteristic of a tabular model in Power BI?

choices.A: It is a multidimensional cube stored in SSAS
choices.B: It consists of tables with columns, relationships, hierarchies, and calculations
choices.C: It only supports flat file data sources
choices.D: It cannot contain calculated columns or measures

questions.explanation: A Power BI model is a tabular model meaning it is structured as tables with columns, supports relationships between tables, hierarchies, and custom calculations (measures and calculated columns).

questions.question: In a star schema, what is the role of the fact table?

choices.A: Describes business entities such as customers or products
choices.B: Stores keys linking to dimension tables and numeric measures like sales amounts
choices.C: Acts as a lookup table for filtering dimensions
choices.D: Contains only text fields used for labeling

questions.explanation: The fact table stores measurable, quantitative data such as sales orders or transactions. It contains foreign keys linking to dimension tables and columns for numeric measures. Dimension tables describe entities.

questions.question: Which of the following storage modes allows Power BI to decide dynamically whether to query cached data or the data source?

choices.A: Import
choices.B: DirectQuery
choices.C: Dual
choices.D: Composite

questions.explanation: Dual storage mode allows tables to be queried from cached data (like Import) or directly from the source (like DirectQuery), with Power BI optimizing for performance.

questions.question: A composite model is defined as:

choices.A: A model where all tables use Import storage mode
choices.B: A model with tables all set to DirectQuery mode from the same source
choices.C: A model combining tables with different storage modes or multiple source groups
choices.D: A model that only uses calculated tables

questions.explanation: Composite models mix tables with different storage modes (Import, DirectQuery) or come from multiple data sources (source groups).

questions.question: Which of the following statements about filters in analytic queries is TRUE?

choices.A: Filter values are always visible in the query result
choices.B: Filters can be applied at the report, page, or visual level in Power BI reports
choices.C: Row-Level Security (RLS) is unrelated to filtering
choices.D: Measures cannot apply filters

questions.explanation: Filters can be applied at various levels in Power BI reports (report, page, visual). Filter values themselves are generally not visible in the query results. RLS is a security filter applied to data access and measures can apply filters using DAX.

questions.question: Which language(s) does Power BI use for querying models?

choices.A: Only DAX
choices.B: Only MDX
choices.C: DAX for Power BI reports; MDX for paginated reports and Analyze in Excel
choices.D: SQL only

questions.explanation: Power BI reports use DAX; paginated reports and Excel’s Analyze in Excel use MDX. SQL is used at the data source level, not within the model queries.

questions.question: When designing a Power BI model, why is adopting a star schema beneficial?

choices.A: It simplifies the model by using a single large table
choices.B: It improves performance and usability by separating dimensions and facts
choices.C: It removes the need for relationships between tables
choices.D: It only works for models with fewer than 10 tables

questions.explanation: The star schema organizes data into fact tables and dimension tables, optimizing query performance and making the model easier to understand and maintain.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a phase of an analytic query in Power BI?

choices.A: Filter
choices.B: Group
choices.C: Aggregate
choices.D: Summarize

questions.explanation: The three phases are Filter, Group, and Summarize. 'Aggregate' is not named as a separate phase; aggregation happens during summarization.

questions.question: What does the source group refer to in the context of Power BI models?

choices.A: The collection of tables with the same storage mode setting
choices.B: The collection of tables that come from the same data source in a DirectQuery model
choices.C: A security group controlling access to datasets
choices.D: The set of calculated tables in a model

questions.explanation: A source group is a set of tables that originate from the same data source, particularly relevant for DirectQuery models.

questions.question: Why might you use DirectQuery mode instead of Import mode for a Power BI table?

choices.A: When you want faster query performance with cached data
choices.B: When the data changes frequently and must reflect real-time updates
choices.C: When you want to avoid complex queries
choices.D: When data size is very small

questions.explanation: DirectQuery mode keeps data at the source and queries live data on-demand, ideal for scenarios requiring up-to-date data.

questions.question: In Power BI, what is the primary difference between a calculated table and other tables in terms of storage mode?

choices.A: Calculated tables have no storage mode property
choices.B: Calculated tables are always stored as Import
choices.C: Calculated tables cannot have relationships
choices.D: Calculated tables use DirectQuery only

questions.explanation: Calculated tables don’t have a storage mode property because they are computed within the model itself, rather than being imported or queried from an external source.

questions.question: How does row-level security (RLS) interact with filters in an analytic query?

choices.A: RLS is applied before the filter phase and restricts data access
choices.B: RLS applies after summarization
choices.C: RLS replaces the grouping phase
choices.D: RLS only affects DirectQuery models

questions.explanation: RLS filters data before the query processes, restricting the rows visible to the user based on their permissions. It is independent of storage mode.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about hybrid datasets is true?

choices.A: Hybrid datasets combine Import and DirectQuery modes within the same table
choices.B: Hybrid datasets combine multiple source groups in a composite model
choices.C: Hybrid datasets are streaming datasets combined with push datasets
choices.D: Hybrid datasets always require MDX queries

questions.explanation: Hybrid datasets refer to composite models with tables from different source groups, possibly combining Import and DirectQuery modes across tables.

questions.question: What happens if you apply a slicer filter in a Power BI report?

choices.A: It applies a visible filter that affects the entire report including all pages
choices.B: It applies a filter only on the page or visual where the slicer is placed
choices.C: It applies an invisible filter narrowing down data used by visuals on the report page
choices.D: It disables the summarization phase of analytic queries

questions.explanation: A slicer applies a filter that narrows the data subset for visuals, but the filter values themselves aren’t directly shown in the visuals.

questions.question: In the context of Power BI, which scenario best illustrates grouping (dicing) in an analytic query?

choices.A: Filtering sales data to a specific year
choices.B: Summarizing total sales across all customers
choices.C: Displaying sales broken down by customer segment
choices.D: Importing data from Excel

questions.explanation: Grouping (dicing) divides the data into visible groups such as customer segments, so the output shows summarized values per group.

questions.question: What is a composite model in Power BI?

choices.A: A model that uses only DirectQuery storage mode
choices.B: A model that combines data from multiple tables with the same storage mode
choices.C: A model that combines more than one source group, typically import and DirectQuery
choices.D: A model that only uses imported data

questions.explanation: A composite model combines data from more than one source group, typically mixing import and DirectQuery storage modes. This allows balancing performance and freshness. Options A, B, and D describe models with a single storage mode, so they do not qualify as composite models.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key benefit of using composite models?

choices.A: Eliminates the need for data refresh
choices.B: Provides design flexibility by combining import and DirectQuery storage modes
choices.C: Guarantees no performance impact when combining queries from different sources
choices.D: Removes the need for relationships between tables

questions.explanation: Composite models offer design flexibility by allowing a mix of imported and DirectQuery data, optimizing performance and data freshness. Imported data still requires refresh (A is false), combining queries can impact performance (C is false), and relationships are still needed (D is false).

questions.question: What limitation must you consider when combining imported data with DirectQuery tables?

choices.A: Imported data automatically syncs with DirectQuery data in real time
choices.B: Combining queries across source groups requires result consolidation, which can impact performance
choices.C: Relationships between imported and DirectQuery tables are always unlimited
choices.D: Imported data never requires refreshing

questions.explanation: When queries combine imported and DirectQuery tables, Power BI must consolidate results from different source groups, which can slow performance. Imported data does not sync automatically (A false), relationships are often limited (C false), and imported data needs periodic refresh (D false).

questions.question: What does setting a table to "dual storage mode" enable?

choices.A: The table stores data only in DirectQuery mode
choices.B: The table dynamically chooses between import and DirectQuery modes at query time
choices.C: The table automatically disables incremental refresh
choices.D: The table cannot be used in slicers or filters

questions.explanation: Dual storage mode allows a table to operate in both import and DirectQuery modes. Power BI decides the most efficient mode at query time, often answering queries from cached data, improving performance.

questions.question: Why might you add import aggregation tables in a composite model?

choices.A: To force all queries to be answered by DirectQuery
choices.B: To cache higher-grain aggregations and improve query performance
choices.C: To eliminate the need for dual storage mode on dimension tables
choices.D: To prevent periodic refresh of imported data

questions.explanation: Import aggregation tables store pre-aggregated data in import mode, which helps Power BI respond quickly to high-level queries without querying the source live. This boosts performance without eliminating refresh needs or forcing DirectQuery.

questions.question: What are “limited relationships” in composite models?

choices.A: Relationships that always have a guaranteed "one" side with unique values
choices.B: Relationships spanning different source groups or with many-to-many cardinality, which can affect query evaluation
choices.C: Relationships that can only exist between tables in the same source group
choices.D: Relationships that are automatically optimized by Power BI without any restrictions

questions.explanation: Limited relationships happen when relationships span different source groups or have many-to-many cardinality. They can affect query and calculation evaluation. Option A is incorrect as limited relationships do not guarantee uniqueness.

questions.question: How does Power BI deliver real-time data in an import model with incremental refresh?

choices.A: By disabling DirectQuery and refreshing all data on every query
choices.B: By enabling “Get the latest data in real-time with DirectQuery,” creating a hybrid table with both import and DirectQuery partitions
choices.C: By forcing all data to be stored only in DirectQuery mode
choices.D: By requiring manual refreshes every minute

questions.explanation: Enabling this option creates a hybrid table storing older data in import partitions and current data in a DirectQuery partition. Queries use cached data for older records and live queries for recent data, providing real-time updates efficiently. This feature requires a Premium license.

questions.question: What potential risk exists when chaining DirectQuery to Power BI datasets in composite models?

choices.A: It eliminates the need for data refresh
choices.B: Changes in upstream models can break downstream models without impact analysis
choices.C: It improves performance regardless of dataset changes
choices.D: It automatically converts all tables to import mode

questions.explanation: Chaining models can cause dependencies where changes upstream may break downstream datasets. It is important to perform dataset impact analysis before making changes. The other options are false or irrelevant.

questions.question: Which feature is required to use automatic aggregations with composite models?

choices.A: Power BI Pro license
choices.B: Power BI Premium license
choices.C: Free Power BI account
choices.D: No special license, available to all users

questions.explanation: Automatic aggregations are a Premium feature, requiring a Power BI Premium license.

questions.question: Which of these statements about slicers and filter cards in composite models is true?

choices.A: They always query data live from the source using DirectQuery
choices.B: They render more slowly when using dual storage mode tables
choices.C: They typically render faster when based on columns in dual storage mode dimension tables because cached data is used
choices.D: They cannot be used with composite models

questions.explanation: Slicers and filter cards on dimension tables set to dual storage mode render faster because queries are answered from cached data instead of live queries.

questions.question: Which model framework should you choose to ensure the best performance and most design flexibility for a typical enterprise Power BI report?

choices.A: DirectQuery
choices.B: Import
choices.C: Composite
choices.D: Live Connection

questions.explanation: The Import model framework is recommended whenever possible because it offers the best performance by loading data into Power BI, and provides the most design flexibility. DirectQuery queries data at runtime, which may slow down performance. Composite models combine features but add complexity. Live Connection is used for external models, not described here.

questions.question: Which of the following is true regarding conversions between table storage modes in Power BI Desktop?

choices.A: You can convert an Import table to a DirectQuery table anytime.
choices.B: You cannot convert a DirectQuery table to an Import table.
choices.C: You can convert a DirectQuery table to an Import table, but not vice versa.
choices.D: You can convert Import and DirectQuery tables interchangeably without restrictions.

questions.explanation: Power BI Desktop allows converting a DirectQuery table to an Import table to improve performance or reduce real-time dependencies, but it does NOT allow converting an Import table back to DirectQuery. This makes the initial choice important.

questions.question: When is the DirectQuery model framework most appropriate?

choices.A: When you want to load minimal data into Power BI for best query speed.
choices.B: When your data source has very large volumes and you need near real-time data.
choices.C: When you want to combine data from multiple sources into a single dataset.
choices.D: When you want to extend an existing Power BI dataset with additional data.

questions.explanation: DirectQuery is best when the data source contains very large data volumes and the report requires near real-time data, because data is queried directly on the source without importing. Options A is more about Import models, and D relates more to composite models.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of using aggregation tables in a DirectQuery model?

choices.A: They allow you to import the entire dataset for faster queries.
choices.B: They improve query performance by serving higher-level aggregations from cache.
choices.C: They enable Power BI to bypass the source system completely.
choices.D: They replace the need for dimension tables.

questions.explanation: Aggregation tables store pre-calculated summaries, either in Import or DirectQuery mode, to improve query performance. When dimension tables use dual mode, queries can be answered from cache, reducing source hits.

questions.question: How can you deliver near real-time query results from an Import model?

choices.A: By using only DirectQuery tables.
choices.B: By creating a hybrid table with a DirectQuery partition for the current period.
choices.C: By switching all tables to DirectQuery mode.
choices.D: By refreshing the dataset every hour manually.

questions.explanation: Hybrid tables combine imported historical data with a DirectQuery partition for current data, enabling near real-time querying while keeping the benefits of Import for older data.

questions.question: What does setting dimension tables to dual storage mode achieve when using import aggregation tables?

choices.A: It disables caching for all related queries.
choices.B: It allows queries to be answered fully from cache when possible.
choices.C: It forces Power BI to always use DirectQuery for those tables.
choices.D: It reduces data volume by compressing dimension tables.

questions.explanation: Dual storage mode enables tables to act as Import (cached) or DirectQuery depending on query context. This allows many queries to be served from cache, greatly improving performance.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the role of a business analyst in extending Power BI core models using DirectQuery?

choices.A: They create core datasets used by IT.
choices.B: They extend existing core models by chaining with DirectQuery connections.
choices.C: They build all models from scratch without IT involvement.
choices.D: They only create Import models for better flexibility.

questions.explanation: Business analysts often extend core models delivered by IT by chaining via DirectQuery connections, adding additional data or logic without changing the core dataset.

questions.question: What is a recommended practice to improve performance when using the Import model?

choices.A: Import the entire dataset regardless of size.
choices.B: Apply data reduction techniques to load only necessary data.
choices.C: Always use DirectQuery instead of Import.
choices.D: Use only composite models.

questions.explanation: Reducing the amount of data imported (filtering, partitions) improves Import model performance and load times by minimizing data volume.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of the composite model framework?

choices.A: Boost the query performance of a DirectQuery model.
choices.B: Deliver near real-time query results from an Import model.
choices.C: Extend a Power BI dataset or AAS model with additional data.
choices.D: Automatically convert Import tables to DirectQuery tables.

questions.explanation: Composite models improve DirectQuery performance, enable near real-time data with Import, and extend datasets, but they do not automatically convert Import tables to DirectQuery.

questions.question: Why is careful planning important when choosing a model framework in Power BI?

choices.A: Because converting Import tables to DirectQuery is simple and reversible.
choices.B: Because you cannot convert Import tables to DirectQuery tables once imported.
choices.C: Because DirectQuery always offers better performance.
choices.D: Because composite models do not support real-time data.

questions.explanation: Once a table is imported, you cannot convert it back to DirectQuery. This limitation means planning is crucial to meet data freshness and performance requirements.
