questions.question: Which of the following statements about connecting to data sources in Power BI is TRUE?

choices.A: Power BI only supports connecting to relational databases like SQL Server.
choices.B: Power Query is used to clean and transform data after loading it into reports.
choices.C: Power Query can connect to multiple types of data sources, including relational databases, files, and cloud services.
choices.D: Azure Analysis Services stores data exclusively in Excel files.

questions.explanation: Power Query is a versatile data connection and transformation tool that supports many types of data sources — relational databases (SQL Server), files (Excel), applications (Cosmos DB), and cloud services (Azure Analysis Services). Option A is false because Power BI supports more than just relational databases. Option B is incorrect because Power Query transforms data before it is loaded into reports. Option D is incorrect; Azure Analysis Services stores analytical models, not Excel files.

questions.question: Tailwind Traders’ sales database contains details about sales transactions but lacks employee hire date and manager info. Where should this missing data be sourced from?

choices.A: Microsoft SQL Server
choices.B: Microsoft Excel files from Human Resources
choices.C: Cosmos DB JSON documents
choices.D: Azure Analysis Services projections

questions.explanation: Employee hire date, title, and manager information are maintained by HR in Excel files, which is why you need to connect to those Excel files separately. SQL Server only contains sales transactions and some employee identifiers but not their HR details. Cosmos DB contains shipment data, and Azure Analysis Services holds sales projections.

questions.question: Which storage mode in Power BI is best suited for data that changes frequently and requires near real-time reporting?

choices.A: Import Mode
choices.B: DirectQuery Mode
choices.C: Dual Mode
choices.D: Excel Mode

questions.explanation: DirectQuery mode allows Power BI to query the data source directly each time a report is refreshed, making it suitable for frequently changing data that needs near real-time updates. Import mode imports data into Power BI, which can be out-of-date until refreshed. Dual mode combines both. "Excel Mode" is not a Power BI storage mode.

questions.question: When combining data from multiple sources like SQL Server, Excel, and Cosmos DB, which Power BI tool helps you to clean and shape this data before building reports?

choices.A: Power Pivot
choices.B: Power Query
choices.C: Power View
choices.D: Power Automate

questions.explanation: Power Query is the ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) tool in Power BI for connecting, cleaning, transforming, and combining data before it is used in reports. Power Pivot is mainly for data modeling, Power View is for visualizations, and Power Automate is for automation workflows.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical data transformation you would perform in Power Query?

choices.A: Renaming columns
choices.B: Replacing values
choices.C: Building a semantic data model
choices.D: Removing errors from data

questions.explanation: Building a semantic data model happens after data is cleaned and loaded, typically in Power BI Desktop’s data modeling view. Renaming columns, replacing values, and removing errors are common Power Query transformations.

questions.question: What kind of data format does Cosmos DB store, which is used for shipment records at Tailwind Traders?

choices.A: Relational tables
choices.B: XML files
choices.C: JSON documents
choices.D: CSV files

questions.explanation: Cosmos DB is a NoSQL database that stores data as JSON documents. It is designed for flexible, hierarchical data storage, unlike relational tables. XML or CSV are not native Cosmos DB formats.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of publishing a semantic model and reports to Power BI Service?

choices.A: Only the original creator can view the reports
choices.B: It allows others to reuse the semantic model and create their own reports
choices.C: It disables report editing for everyone
choices.D: Reports are automatically exported to Excel

questions.explanation: Publishing to Power BI Service enables collaboration. Other users can build reports on top of the shared semantic model or use existing reports. It promotes reusability and sharing, unlike options A or C. Exporting to Excel (D) is not automatic.

questions.question: What should you do if you encounter performance issues after importing large datasets into Power BI?

choices.A: Delete unnecessary columns and filter rows during the Power Query transformation
choices.B: Import all available data without filtering to ensure completeness
choices.C: Use only Excel files as data sources
choices.D: Avoid using Power Query transformations

questions.explanation: To improve performance, it’s best to reduce data size by filtering rows and removing unnecessary columns during the Power Query step. Importing all data can slow down reports. Using only Excel or avoiding transformations is not practical or helpful.

questions.question: Which statement best describes Azure Analysis Services in the Tailwind Traders scenario?

choices.A: It stores transactional sales data in JSON format.
choices.B: It contains financial projections to predict future sales trends.
choices.C: It is a file-based data source like Excel.
choices.D: It manages employee data such as hire dates and managers.

questions.explanation: Azure Analysis Services is used to store analytical models, such as financial sales projections in this scenario. It does not store transactional or employee data nor is it a file-based source.

questions.question: Why might the HR department at Tailwind Traders still be using Excel instead of SQL Server for employee data?

choices.A: SQL Server cannot store employee data
choices.B: Excel is more secure than SQL Server
choices.C: HR hasn’t yet migrated their data to SQL Server
choices.D: Cosmos DB replaced Excel for HR data

questions.explanation: The text states that HR hasn’t had the chance to implement a SQL database yet, so they continue to use Excel files. SQL Server can store employee data, and Excel is generally less secure. Cosmos DB is used for shipment data, not HR.

questions.question: What is the main difference between relational databases (e.g., SQL Server) and Cosmos DB in the context of Power BI?

choices.A: SQL Server stores data as tables, Cosmos DB stores data as JSON documents
choices.B: Cosmos DB is only used for financial projections
choices.C: SQL Server cannot handle large volumes of data
choices.D: Cosmos DB requires Power Pivot to connect

questions.explanation: SQL Server is a relational database storing data in structured tables with rows and columns. Cosmos DB is a NoSQL database that stores data as flexible JSON documents, making it ideal for hierarchical or semi-structured data like shipment records.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the role of a semantic model in Power BI?

choices.A: A tool to clean data in Power Query
choices.B: A visual report created from raw data
choices.C: A structured model combining data from multiple sources for analysis
choices.D: An Excel workbook used for data storage

questions.explanation: A semantic model is a logical, structured representation of combined data from various sources, designed to facilitate reporting and analysis. It acts as a layer between raw data and reports.

questions.question: During Power Query data transformation, which action would best help to resolve errors during data import?

choices.A: Use the "Remove Errors" option to exclude rows with errors
choices.B: Ignore errors and proceed with data import
choices.C: Delete the entire query and start over
choices.D: Convert all data to text format

questions.explanation: Power Query allows you to detect and remove rows with errors, ensuring clean data is loaded. Ignoring errors or deleting queries is inefficient. Converting all data to text doesn’t solve the root causes.

questions.question: Why is it important to understand the nuances of each data source before connecting with Power Query?

choices.A: Because every data source has unique connection methods, data formats, and refresh capabilities
choices.B: It is not important; all data sources are connected the same way in Power BI
choices.C: Only SQL Server requires special handling in Power Query
choices.D: Power Query only works with Excel and CSV files

questions.explanation: Different data sources like SQL Server, Excel, Cosmos DB, and Azure Analysis Services have different connection protocols, data structures, and refresh limitations. Understanding these helps optimize data retrieval and processing.

questions.question: What does selecting an appropriate storage mode in Power BI impact?

choices.A: The color scheme of reports
choices.B: Performance, data freshness, and how data queries are processed
choices.C: The size of Excel files connected
choices.D: The number of reports you can publish

questions.explanation: Storage modes such as Import or DirectQuery influence how quickly data loads, how fresh the data is, and whether queries run on the source system or on the imported data model, directly affecting performance.

questions.question: Which of the following is TRUE about the Power BI service after publishing reports?

choices.A: Reports are static and cannot be modified by users
choices.B: Only people with Power BI Desktop can view reports
choices.C: Users can create new reports based on published semantic models
choices.D: Power BI service deletes all underlying data sources after publishing

questions.explanation: Published semantic models can be reused by other users to create new reports in the Power BI service, facilitating collaboration. Reports are interactive and accessible via browser.

questions.question: When would you prefer to use Power Query in Excel instead of Power BI?

choices.A: When creating simple data transformations for Excel reports
choices.B: When needing to publish to Power BI Service directly
choices.C: When connecting to Azure Analysis Services only
choices.D: When building semantic models for large datasets

questions.explanation: Power Query in Excel is ideal for cleaning and transforming data within Excel for analysis there. Power BI is better suited for building comprehensive reports and models and publishing them online.

questions.question: What is the benefit of combining query results in Power Query?

choices.A: To create a single unified dataset from multiple sources for easier analysis
choices.B: To delete unnecessary queries
choices.C: To export data to CSV files automatically
choices.D: To format reports visually

questions.explanation: Combining queries merges data from multiple sources into one dataset, making it easier to analyze and visualize in reports. The other options are unrelated.

questions.question: If an error occurs during data import from a data source in Power BI, what is the recommended troubleshooting step?

choices.A: Check the data types and formats in the source system
choices.B: Immediately delete the data source connection
choices.C: Disable Power Query transformations
choices.D: Restart your computer

questions.explanation: Errors often stem from data type mismatches or unexpected formats. Checking and correcting these at the source or during transformation helps resolve import issues effectively.

questions.question: What is the first step you must perform before creating reports in Power BI using multiple data sources?

choices.A: Build dashboards directly from raw data
choices.B: Extract and clean data from the various sources using Power Query
choices.C: Publish semantic models without data preparation
choices.D: Connect only to Excel files

questions.explanation: The initial and essential step is to extract, clean, and organize data from all relevant sources using Power Query before building reports. This ensures data consistency and quality.

questions.question: Which Power BI feature allows reports and models created by one user to be reused and extended by others?

choices.A: Power BI Desktop
choices.B: Semantic Model published to Power BI Service
choices.C: Power Query Editor
choices.D: Azure Analysis Services

questions.explanation: Publishing the semantic model to Power BI Service enables collaboration where multiple users can build on and extend existing models and reports.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a flat file in the context of Power BI data sources?

choices.A: A file containing multiple tables with hierarchical relationships
choices.B: A file containing a single table with uniform row structure and no hierarchies
choices.C: A file that is always stored in the cloud and auto-updated in Power BI
choices.D: A file exclusively in Excel .xlsx format

questions.explanation: A flat file contains only one table where every row follows the same structure and there are no hierarchies or nested data. It includes file types like .csv and .txt. Option A is incorrect because flat files do not have multiple related tables. Option C describes cloud storage syncing but not flat file structure. Option D is wrong because flat files are not exclusively Excel files.

questions.question: When importing data from a local Excel file in Power BI Desktop, what happens when the original Excel file is modified after import?

choices.A: Power BI automatically detects and applies the changes in real-time
choices.B: Power BI creates a link and updates the data every time you open the report
choices.C: Power BI does not reflect changes made to the original file after import
choices.D: Power BI blocks you from importing files stored locally

questions.explanation: When importing from a local file, Power BI creates a semantic model and imports the data once. There is no connection or sync afterward, so changes in the source file do not update the Power BI dataset automatically. Auto-sync is only available when files are stored in cloud locations like OneDrive or SharePoint.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about using OneDrive for Business as a data source is FALSE?

choices.A: Power BI connects regularly to OneDrive for Business files to keep data synchronized
choices.B: Changes in Excel files on OneDrive for Business automatically update Power BI reports and dashboards
choices.C: Files stored on OneDrive for Business cannot be accessed by multiple users simultaneously
choices.D: Using OneDrive for Business helps keep Power BI semantic models in sync with source files

questions.explanation: OneDrive for Business supports collaborative access, allowing multiple users to work on files simultaneously. Therefore, option C is false. Options A, B, and D correctly describe the advantages of OneDrive for Business for data syncing with Power BI.

questions.question: You have a Power BI report connected to an Excel file stored on SharePoint Team Sites. If the file is moved to a different folder within the same SharePoint site, what must you do in Power BI to ensure the report continues working?

choices.A: Nothing; Power BI automatically tracks the new file location
choices.B: Re-import the Excel file from the new folder location as a new dataset
choices.C: Update the file path in the Data Source Settings to point to the new location
choices.D: Save the report to OneDrive instead

questions.explanation: Power BI does not automatically detect file moves or renames. You need to update the file path in Data Source Settings to maintain the connection. Option A is false because no automatic tracking occurs. Option B is unnecessary if you update the path correctly. Option D is unrelated to fixing the broken path.

questions.question: In Power BI Desktop, after selecting an Excel file to import, what is the purpose of the Navigator window?

choices.A: To edit the data using M language before loading
choices.B: To display available tables and preview their contents before loading or transforming
choices.C: To automatically load all tables without user selection
choices.D: To permanently link the Excel file to Power BI reports

questions.explanation: The Navigator window allows users to preview available tables/entities from the data source and select which ones to load or transform. It does not edit M code (that is done in the Advanced Editor). It also does not force automatic loading (option C), nor does it create a permanent link (option D).

questions.question: Which Power BI feature should you use to clean and shape your data before loading it into the model?

choices.A: Data Source Settings
choices.B: Navigator Window
choices.C: Power Query Editor
choices.D: Advanced Editor

questions.explanation: The Power Query Editor is the tool designed for data transformation, cleaning, and shaping before loading data into the Power BI model. The Data Source Settings manage connections, the Navigator helps select tables, and the Advanced Editor is used for advanced query script editing inside Power Query.

questions.question: If your source Excel file’s structure changes (e.g., columns are deleted or renamed), what is the likely impact on your Power BI reports?

choices.A: The reports automatically adjust to the new structure without issues
choices.B: The data will fail to load or the reports will break due to schema mismatch
choices.C: Power BI prompts you to update the file structure automatically
choices.D: The changed columns will be ignored, and the rest will load normally

questions.explanation: Power BI depends on the file’s schema (column names, order, types). Structural changes such as renaming or deleting columns will cause errors in queries or break visuals that depend on those fields. Power BI does not automatically adapt or ignore these changes.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended practice when changing the source file path in Power BI?

choices.A: Ensuring the new file has the same structure as the original
choices.B: Using the Change Source option in Data Source Settings
choices.C: Loading the data again without changing the source path
choices.D: Verifying the connection after updating the file path

questions.explanation: Loading data again without updating the source path when the file has moved or changed location will cause errors. It is essential to use the Change Source option and verify the new connection. The other options are correct best practices.

questions.question: Which type of data import scenario is most suitable for files that rarely change?

choices.A: OneDrive for Business connection
choices.B: SharePoint Team Sites connection
choices.C: Importing from a local file on your computer
choices.D: Using a live connection to a database

questions.explanation: Importing from a local file is suitable for data that doesn't change frequently because Power BI does not sync changes automatically. Cloud-based options (OneDrive, SharePoint) are better for frequently updated data. Live connections are for databases, not flat files.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of storing Power BI data source files on cloud services like OneDrive or SharePoint?

choices.A: They allow you to edit Power BI reports directly from the cloud
choices.B: They eliminate the need to use Power Query Editor
choices.C: They enable automatic synchronization between the source files and Power BI semantic models
choices.D: They prevent data from being imported into Power BI Desktop

questions.explanation: Storing source files on OneDrive or SharePoint allows Power BI to regularly check for changes and automatically update semantic models, reports, and dashboards, ensuring synchronization. Options A, B, and D are incorrect or unrelated to this benefit.

questions.question: In Power BI Desktop, where can you find the “Get data” option to import files such as Excel or CSV?

choices.A: View tab
choices.B: Home tab
choices.C: Insert tab
choices.D: Modeling tab

questions.explanation: The Get data feature is located on the Home tab in Power BI Desktop, providing quick access to import data from various sources.

questions.question: When connecting to a personal OneDrive account in Power BI, what must you do to ensure the connection remains active?

choices.A: Disable “Keep me signed in” for security
choices.B: Sign in and select “Keep me signed in” option
choices.C: No login is required for personal OneDrive accounts
choices.D: Use a work email instead

questions.explanation: To maintain an active connection with OneDrive Personal files, you must sign in and select the “Keep me signed in” option; otherwise, the connection may drop and require reauthentication.

questions.question: What does Power BI do when you import data from a local file (e.g., Excel) stored on your computer?

choices.A: Moves the file into Power BI storage
choices.B: Creates a live link to the file and updates dynamically
choices.C: Creates a new semantic model and loads data from the file without keeping a live link
choices.D: Uploads the file to OneDrive automatically

questions.explanation: Power BI does not move or link the local file but creates a semantic model by loading the data once. It does not sync changes made in the original file after import.

questions.question: In the Navigator window after selecting a file in Power BI Desktop, what options do you have before importing?

choices.A: Load data directly or transform data in Power Query Editor
choices.B: Only load data without any preview
choices.C: Transform data but cannot load it
choices.D: Edit the file externally before import

questions.explanation: The Navigator window lets you preview available tables, then choose to either Load data directly or Transform Data using Power Query Editor for cleaning/shaping.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about cloud file storage sync with Power BI is TRUE?

choices.A: Power BI stores a separate copy of your OneDrive files offline
choices.B: Power BI checks OneDrive and SharePoint files regularly to sync updates automatically
choices.C: Changes in OneDrive files require manual re-import into Power BI
choices.D: SharePoint Team Sites do not support file connections for Power BI

questions.explanation: Power BI regularly connects to files stored on OneDrive for Business or SharePoint Team Sites to detect changes and automatically update semantic models and reports.

questions.question: Which of the following authentication methods can be used when connecting Power BI Desktop to an on-premises SQL Server database? (Select all that apply)

choices.A: Windows Authentication (Azure Active Directory credentials)
choices.B: OAuth Authentication
choices.C: Database Authentication (SQL Server credentials)
choices.D: Microsoft Account Authentication

questions.explanation: Power BI Desktop supports Windows Authentication (Azure AD), Database Authentication (SQL Server credentials), and Microsoft Account Authentication (mainly for Azure). OAuth Authentication is not a standard option for on-premises SQL Server.

questions.question: When connecting Power BI to a SQL Server, which data connectivity mode is recommended for most scenarios, and why?

choices.A: DirectQuery, because it imports all data immediately
choices.B: Import, because it creates a cached copy in Power BI improving performance
choices.C: DirectQuery, because it allows offline work
choices.D: Import, because it only queries the database in real-time

questions.explanation: Import mode pulls data into Power BI’s internal data model, making report performance faster since queries run locally. DirectQuery queries live data and can be slower due to database/network latency. Therefore, Import is generally recommended unless near-real-time data is required.

questions.question: Which of the following are advantages of writing SQL queries directly in Power BI’s SQL Server database connector?

choices.A: Import only required columns and rows, reducing data size
choices.B: Improve report performance by minimizing data imported
choices.C: Avoid using WHERE clauses to speed up data loading
choices.D: Join tables and perform calculations before data import

questions.explanation: Writing SQL queries lets you select specific columns and rows, reducing unnecessary data, improving performance. You can also join tables and run calculations before import. Avoiding WHERE clauses is incorrect; WHERE clauses help filter data efficiently.

questions.question: Why is using the wildcard character (*) in a SELECT statement discouraged when importing data into Power BI?

choices.A: It imports all columns, possibly including unnecessary data
choices.B: It improves query performance by retrieving all data at once
choices.C: It causes redundant data leading to larger Power BI file sizes
choices.D: It makes data modeling and report maintenance more complex

questions.explanation: Using SELECT * imports every column including irrelevant ones, leading to larger files and slower performance, and complicates data modeling and maintenance. It does not improve performance.

questions.question: You have connected to a SQL Server database and imported sales data. The database password needs to be updated every 90 days. Which Power BI feature allows you to update your connection credentials without recreating the connection?

choices.A: Refresh Now
choices.B: Data source settings
choices.C: Transform Data > Query Editor
choices.D: Power BI Service Gateway

questions.explanation: The Data source settings in Power BI Desktop allow you to update credentials, change or clear permissions without recreating connections. Refresh triggers data reload but doesn’t update credentials. Transform Data is for shaping data, and Gateway relates to service refreshes.

questions.question: What is “Query Folding” in the context of Power BI and relational databases?

choices.A: A technique to compress data after import
choices.B: Power Query’s ability to translate transformations back to source SQL queries
choices.C: The process of manually writing SQL queries for import
choices.D: A Power BI visualization feature that groups queries

questions.explanation: Query Folding means Power Query translates transformation steps back into SQL queries that are run on the source database, improving efficiency and reducing data load. It is not about compression, manual SQL, or visualization.

questions.question: In which cases would you prefer to use a SQL View over embedding a complex SQL query directly inside Power BI?

choices.A: When you want to centralize business logic in the database for reuse
choices.B: When you want to allow Query Folding and improve performance
choices.C: When you want to avoid writing any SQL
choices.D: When the database administrator wants to control data access policies

questions.explanation: SQL Views centralize logic for reuse, allow better Query Folding and performance, and let DBAs control access and optimizations. You still need SQL to create views, so avoiding SQL entirely is not possible.

questions.question: What happens if you select multiple tables in the Navigator window and click “Load” without transforming the data?

choices.A: Power BI imports all selected tables as-is into the data model
choices.B: Power BI opens Power Query for data shaping automatically
choices.C: Data is imported only if you have written an SQL query
choices.D: Power BI creates relationships automatically between tables

questions.explanation: Clicking Load imports selected tables directly without opening Power Query. Transformations happen only if you select Transform Data. Relationships may be auto-detected but are not guaranteed. SQL query writing is optional.

questions.question: What are the potential consequences of importing unfiltered historical sales data that is not relevant to the report?

choices.A: Larger data models that slow down report performance
choices.B: Increased storage requirements in Power BI files
choices.C: Faster report refresh due to more data being available
choices.D: More complex data model requiring additional normalization

questions.explanation: Importing irrelevant data increases model size, storage, and complexity, slowing performance. It does not speed up refresh; it actually slows it down.

questions.question: Which Power BI window allows you to preview data from the connected database before importing?

choices.A: Data source settings
choices.B: Navigator
choices.C: Power Query Editor
choices.D: SQL Server Management Studio

questions.explanation: The Navigator window previews tables/entities from the source and lets you select which data to import or transform. Data source settings manage connections, Power Query Editor is for transformation, and SSMS is a separate external tool.

questions.question: In the SQL Server connection window, what is the purpose of the “Advanced options” section?

choices.A: To enter a custom SQL query to filter or transform data before import
choices.B: To choose between Import and DirectQuery modes
choices.C: To set the Windows or Database authentication method
choices.D: To preview the data in tables before import

questions.explanation: The Advanced options section allows you to write a custom SQL query to specify exactly which columns and rows to import, improving efficiency. Import/DirectQuery mode and authentication settings are configured elsewhere.

questions.question: Which of the following actions can you perform in Power Query after loading data from a relational database?

choices.A: Delete unnecessary rows or columns
choices.B: Group data to create summarized tables
choices.C: Remove errors and clean data
choices.D: Change server and database connection details

questions.explanation: Power Query allows extensive data shaping such as deleting rows/columns, grouping data, and cleaning errors. Changing connection details is done via Data source settings, not inside data transformation.

questions.question: How can you modify the data source settings directly from within Power Query?

choices.A: By clicking the gear icon next to the Source step in the Query Settings pane
choices.B: By editing the SQL query in the Advanced Editor
choices.C: By selecting Transform Data > Data source settings
choices.D: By refreshing the query in Power BI Desktop

questions.explanation: Inside Power Query, the gear icon next to the Source step allows editing connection details such as server and database. The Advanced Editor edits query steps, Data source settings is accessed outside Power Query, and refresh only reloads data.

questions.question: Which statement about the “Load” vs “Transform Data” options in Navigator is correct?

choices.A: Load imports data immediately without any transformation
choices.B: Transform Data opens Power Query Editor to allow data shaping before import
choices.C: Transform Data also loads data into the model automatically
choices.D: Load always uses DirectQuery mode

questions.explanation: Load imports selected data immediately as-is. Transform Data opens Power Query for shaping data before loading. Transform Data does not immediately load data until applied. The data connectivity mode is set separately.

questions.question: What are the consequences of changing data source credentials or server details in Power BI after data has been loaded?

choices.A: You must refresh the data to apply changes
choices.B: Reports automatically update without refresh
choices.C: You may need to re-enter credentials due to security policies
choices.D: Data transformations need to be redone

questions.explanation: After changing connection details, a data refresh is required to load data from the new source. You often must re-enter credentials due to security. Existing transformations remain unless data structure changes.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of using dynamic reports with parameters in Power BI?

choices.A: They allow the creation of multiple reports for each user.
choices.B: They enable a single report to be filtered and reused for different user inputs.
choices.C: They automatically generate visualizations without user interaction.
choices.D: They eliminate the need to connect to databases.

questions.explanation: Dynamic reports use parameters to filter data according to user input, allowing one report to serve multiple purposes. This reduces the number of static reports required, saving time and resources. Options A, C, and D are incorrect because dynamic reports do not multiply reports or remove database connections, nor do they create visuals without interaction.

questions.question: When creating a parameter in Power Query Editor, which type and suggested value options should you select to allow any text input?

choices.A: Type: Number, Suggested Values: List
choices.B: Type: Text, Suggested Values: Any value
choices.C: Type: Boolean, Suggested Values: True or False
choices.D: Type: Date, Suggested Values: Fixed List

questions.explanation: To accept flexible user inputs like salespersons’ names or IDs, the parameter should be of type Text with suggested values set to Any value. This ensures the user can input any string value. Other types (Number, Boolean, Date) are too restrictive or irrelevant here.

questions.question: What must you do in the SQL query within the Advanced Editor to utilize the parameter in filtering data?

choices.A: Remove all WHERE clauses from the SQL query.
choices.B: Append the parameter with an ampersand (&) in the query string.
choices.C: Replace the entire query with a Power BI formula.
choices.D: Hardcode the parameter value into the SQL query.

questions.explanation: In Power Query’s Advanced Editor, you concatenate the parameter into the SQL query string using an ampersand (&), so Power BI substitutes the parameter value at runtime. This dynamic integration is essential. Options A, C, and D contradict dynamic parameter usage.

questions.question: After creating a parameter and modifying the SQL query, you get a warning about permission to run native queries. What is the correct way to resolve this?

choices.A: Ignore the warning; the query will run anyway.
choices.B: Select Edit Permission and then Run to grant necessary permissions.
choices.C: Delete the query and create a new one.
choices.D: Disable parameter use to avoid native queries.

questions.explanation: Power BI requires explicit permission to execute native database queries for security reasons. You must select Edit Permission and then Run to allow the query. Ignoring or deleting is not a solution, and disabling parameters removes the feature’s benefit.

questions.question: How do you create a dynamic report that filters on multiple values at once?

choices.A: Use a single text parameter and enter multiple values separated by commas.
choices.B: Create a parameter function and invoke it with a list of values imported from Excel.
choices.C: Use multiple individual parameters, one per value.
choices.D: You cannot filter on multiple values dynamically in Power BI.

questions.explanation: For multiple values, you import an Excel table with values (e.g., multiple SalesPersonIDs), create a function based on the original query, then invoke this function on each value. This approach is scalable and dynamic. Option A doesn’t work as a parameter accepts only a single value, C is impractical, and D is false.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a NoSQL database like Azure Cosmos DB?

choices.A: A database that stores data only in tabular relations with fixed schemas
choices.B: A non-relational, flexible database that stores data often in JSON documents
choices.C: A database optimized only for SQL queries and structured data
choices.D: A database that uses only XML format for data storage

questions.explanation: NoSQL databases are non-relational and do not require fixed schemas or tables. Azure Cosmos DB stores data in flexible formats such as JSON documents, allowing nested and dynamic data structures unlike traditional relational databases.

questions.question: When connecting Power BI Desktop to an Azure Cosmos DB instance for the first time, which credentials are mandatory to input?

choices.A: Only the database name and collection name
choices.B: The account endpoint URL and the account key (Primary Key)
choices.C: Just the account username and password
choices.D: The SQL query string for data retrieval

questions.explanation: To connect to Azure Cosmos DB, you need the account endpoint URL (to specify which database instance to connect to) and the account key (usually the Primary Key) from the Azure portal for authentication. Usernames/passwords or SQL queries do not apply here.

questions.question: Why is it necessary to "expand" JSON records in Power Query after importing data from Cosmos DB?

choices.A: To delete unwanted columns
choices.B: To convert nested JSON objects into tabular format suitable for analysis
choices.C: To encrypt the data for security reasons
choices.D: To connect multiple JSON files into one dataset

questions.explanation: JSON data is often nested or hierarchical. The "Expand" operation in Power Query transforms these nested JSON records into flat tables (rows and columns), making the data usable for reporting and analysis in Power BI.

questions.question: Where in the Azure portal can you find the account endpoint URL and Primary Key required to connect Power BI to Cosmos DB?

choices.A: In the Overview blade of the Cosmos DB account
choices.B: In the Keys blade of the Cosmos DB account
choices.C: In the Access Control (IAM) blade
choices.D: In the Diagnostic settings blade

questions.explanation: The Keys blade of your Azure Cosmos DB account contains the endpoint URL and access keys (Primary and Secondary Keys) required to authenticate connections from tools like Power BI.

questions.question: If you load JSON data directly from Cosmos DB into Power BI without any transformation, what issue will you most likely face?

choices.A: Data will load as a fully normalized table immediately
choices.B: Data will be encrypted and unusable
choices.C: Data will be represented as complex Record types, difficult to analyze without expansion
choices.D: Power BI will automatically create relationships between JSON records

questions.explanation: Without transformation, JSON data appears as nested Record or List objects in Power BI, which cannot be directly analyzed. You must expand and normalize these records in Power Query.

questions.question: In the Navigator window of Power BI when connecting to Cosmos DB, what does the preview pane typically show?

choices.A: The exact rows and columns of the database tables
choices.B: A list of Record items representing the JSON documents
choices.C: Only the database schema definitions
choices.D: SQL statements for querying the data

questions.explanation: The preview pane shows JSON documents represented as Record types because Cosmos DB stores data as JSON documents rather than traditional tables.

questions.question: What does unchecking the "Use original column name as prefix" option do when expanding records in Power Query?

choices.A: It renames columns with a prefix related to their parent column
choices.B: It keeps the original nested column names intact
choices.C: It removes the prefix from expanded columns for cleaner column names
choices.D: It deletes the columns after expansion

questions.explanation: Unchecking this option prevents Power Query from adding the parent column name as a prefix to the expanded columns, resulting in simpler and cleaner column names.

questions.question: After importing and transforming data from Cosmos DB, what is the next essential step before using the data in Power BI reports?

choices.A: Refresh the Azure Cosmos DB account keys
choices.B: Close & Apply changes in Power Query to load the data into Power BI Desktop
choices.C: Export the data to Excel first
choices.D: Delete unnecessary records directly from Cosmos DB

questions.explanation: You must click Close & Apply in Power Query Editor to load the transformed data into Power BI Desktop’s data model, making it available for visualization and reporting.

questions.question: Which data formats are most commonly used to transmit data between Cosmos DB and applications such as Power BI?

choices.A: XML and CSV
choices.B: JSON and BSON
choices.C: Plain text files only
choices.D: Binary large objects (BLOBs) only

questions.explanation: JSON is the standard format used by Cosmos DB for data storage and transmission. BSON (Binary JSON) is sometimes used in similar NoSQL contexts, but JSON is the primary relevant format here.

questions.question: How can data from Azure Cosmos DB be combined with other data sources in Power BI?

choices.A: By importing Cosmos DB data and establishing relationships in the Power BI data model
choices.B: By exporting Cosmos DB data to CSV first, then importing CSV separately
choices.C: Data cannot be combined from NoSQL sources with other data sources in Power BI
choices.D: By linking the Azure Cosmos DB portal directly to Excel

questions.explanation: Once data from Cosmos DB is loaded and normalized into Power BI, it appears as tables and can be related to other imported datasets by creating relationships in the data model, enabling integrated reporting.

questions.question: In Power BI Desktop, how do you find the Azure Cosmos DB connector when getting data?

choices.A: Under the Database category
choices.B: Under the Azure category, accessed via “More...” in Get Data
choices.C: Under the File category
choices.D: It is listed directly in the main Get Data menu

questions.explanation: The Azure Cosmos DB connector is found by clicking Get Data > More..., then selecting the Azure category where it is listed.

questions.question: Why are JSON documents considered a good choice for transmitting data between server and web applications?

choices.A: Because JSON documents are binary files
choices.B: Because JSON is a widely supported open standard format for data exchange and is human-readable
choices.C: Because JSON only supports fixed schemas
choices.D: Because JSON is encrypted by default

questions.explanation: JSON is an open standard format, widely supported and human-readable, making it ideal for transmitting data between servers and web applications.

questions.question: When selecting a database or collection in Power BI’s Navigator window, what are two ways to specify the data source?

choices.A: Typing the database and collection name manually or using the Navigator UI to browse and select
choices.B: Importing a CSV file instead
choices.C: Writing SQL queries to retrieve data
choices.D: Only typing the database name without collections

questions.explanation: You can either manually enter the database and collection names or use the Navigator window to browse and select the relevant database and collection visually.

questions.question: What type of data structure does Power BI assign to all records from Cosmos DB upon preview?

choices.A: Table format with rows and columns
choices.B: List type data
choices.C: Record type data representing JSON documents
choices.D: Binary data type

questions.explanation: Power BI represents JSON documents from Cosmos DB as Record types before transformation, which need to be expanded to create tables.

questions.question: Is it possible to relate Cosmos DB data imported into Power BI with data from other sources?

choices.A: No, Cosmos DB data is isolated
choices.B: Yes, once transformed and loaded, it behaves like any other table in Power BI and can be related
choices.C: Only by exporting to Excel first
choices.D: Only by using Power BI Premium features

questions.explanation: Once Cosmos DB data is imported and properly transformed, it becomes part of the Power BI data model and can be linked to other tables for integrated analysis.

questions.question:
When connecting Power BI Desktop to a SharePoint Online List, which part of the SharePoint URL should you enter?

Select the best option:

choices.A: The full URL including the specific list or file path
choices.B: Only the SharePoint site URL without the specific list path
choices.C: The URL of the specific SharePoint file to import
choices.D: Any URL copied from the browser, no modification needed

questions.explanation: Power BI requires only the site URL to establish the connection because once connected, it lists all available lists on that site. Entering the full path or file URL can cause errors. Sometimes you need to remove the last part of the URL to keep only the site address.

questions.question:
After successfully connecting to a SharePoint Online List, what does the Navigator window in Power BI Desktop display?

Select the best option:

choices.A: A preview of all SharePoint documents
choices.B: Only the default SharePoint homepage
choices.C: Tables and entities (lists) available on the SharePoint site
choices.D: The SharePoint site’s user permissions and access logs

questions.explanation: The Navigator window displays tables and entities (typically SharePoint lists) available on the connected SharePoint site. It allows users to select which list(s) to import or transform. It does not show documents or permissions.

questions.question:
What happens if you select "Load" instead of "Transform Data" when importing data from SharePoint into Power BI?

Select the best option:

choices.A: The data is immediately loaded into the Power BI data model without any changes
choices.B: Power Query Editor opens to modify the data before loading
choices.C: The data import is canceled
choices.D: The data is imported as a CSV file to your computer

questions.explanation: Selecting 'Load' imports the selected data directly into the Power BI data model without any transformation. Choosing 'Transform Data' opens Power Query Editor for shaping or filtering data before loading.

questions.question:
What kind of authentication does Power BI Desktop require when connecting to SharePoint Online?

Select the best option:

choices.A: No authentication is required if SharePoint is public
choices.B: Sign in with a Microsoft Account linked to the SharePoint site
choices.C: OAuth token from any online service
choices.D: SharePoint Administrator credentials only

questions.explanation: Power BI requires signing in with a Microsoft Account authorized to access the SharePoint site. This ensures secure and authorized data connection. Public SharePoint sites rarely hold business data.

questions.question:
Why is it beneficial to connect Power BI to multiple online applications’ data, such as SharePoint and Dynamics 365?

Select the best option:

choices.A: To create duplicate datasets in Power BI
choices.B: To combine data from different sources for more meaningful insights
choices.C: To speed up the SharePoint site loading time
choices.D: To automatically create dashboards without user input

questions.explanation: Connecting multiple data sources allows Power BI to merge and analyze data across systems, enabling richer, comprehensive insights that are not possible by analyzing individual data sources alone.

questions.question:
Which of the following is NOT a valid reason to remove the last part of the URL when connecting to SharePoint Online List?

Select the best option:

choices.A: The last part refers to a specific list or file path, which Power BI does not need at connection time
choices.B: Removing it ensures you connect to the SharePoint root site
choices.C: Power BI automatically fetches available lists from the site URL provided
choices.D: To avoid connecting to the wrong SharePoint server

questions.explanation: Removing the last part of the URL is done to point to the SharePoint site root, not to avoid wrong servers. The server is determined by the domain name in the URL, which usually remains the same.

questions.question:
What should you do if you want to clean or filter data from a SharePoint list before loading it into Power BI Desktop?

Select the best option:

choices.A: Select "Load" and edit the data in the report view
choices.B: Open the list in SharePoint and make changes there
choices.C: Select "Transform Data" to open Power Query Editor before loading
choices.D: Export the data as Excel, edit it, then re-import into Power BI

questions.explanation: Selecting 'Transform Data' opens Power Query Editor, the built-in tool to shape, clean, and filter data before loading it into Power BI. This is the most efficient and recommended approach.

questions.question:
What is the primary purpose of the Power BI Desktop’s "Get Data" feature when working with online services?

Select the best option:

choices.A: To export Power BI reports to SharePoint
choices.B: To connect and import data from external online applications into Power BI
choices.C: To backup Power BI datasets online
choices.D: To edit online service configurations

questions.explanation: "Get Data" is the starting point in Power BI Desktop to connect and import data from many sources including online services like SharePoint, OneDrive, and others, for analysis and reporting.

questions.question:
What business value does importing sales goals from SharePoint into Power BI provide?

Select the best option:

choices.A: It helps the sales team communicate via email
choices.B: It allows sales managers to compare goals with actual sales and assess pipeline health
choices.C: It automatically updates SharePoint permissions
choices.D: It creates invoices based on sales goals

questions.explanation: Importing sales goals allows sales managers to analyze and compare planned goals with actual sales data, helping them understand the current health of the sales pipeline and make better decisions.

questions.question:
Why might you need to edit the SharePoint URL before using it in Power BI?

Select the best option:

choices.A: To add your username and password in the URL
choices.B: To remove the last part if it points to a specific list or file, keeping only the site root
choices.C: To convert the URL to an FTP address
choices.D: To shorten it to just the domain name

questions.explanation: Editing the URL by removing the last part (list or file path) ensures that Power BI connects to the SharePoint site root, enabling it to list all available lists for selection.

questions.question:
Which of the following are examples of other online services Power BI can connect to besides SharePoint?

Select the best option:

choices.A: Outlook and Excel Desktop
choices.B: OneDrive, Dynamics 365, Google Analytics
choices.C: Microsoft Word and PowerPoint
choices.D: Local CSV files only

questions.explanation: Power BI supports connecting to various online services including OneDrive, Dynamics 365, and Google Analytics, which help combine data from diverse systems.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Import storage mode in Power BI is FALSE?

choices.A: Data is stored locally in the Power BI file and can be refreshed on schedule.
choices.B: Import mode supports all Power BI features including Q&A and Quick Insights.
choices.C: Data in Import mode is always live and does not require refresh.
choices.D: Import mode is the default mode when creating new Power BI reports.

questions.explanation: Import mode stores a snapshot of the data in Power BI. This data is NOT live by default; it requires manual or scheduled refreshes to update. Only DirectQuery mode provides live data querying without importing a copy.

questions.question: You have a very large dataset that cannot be efficiently imported due to performance constraints. The dataset also requires real-time updates. Which storage mode is most appropriate?

choices.A: Import
choices.B: DirectQuery
choices.C: Dual
choices.D: Aggregation

questions.explanation: DirectQuery does not import the data but queries the source live, making it suitable for very large datasets and real-time updates. Import would be too slow and consume too much memory. Dual mode is more suitable when you want a mix of import and live data.

questions.question: Which of the following is a limitation of using DirectQuery mode?

choices.A: Inability to refresh data on schedule.
choices.B: Dependence on source system performance during queries.
choices.C: Data is cached in Power BI for faster access.
choices.D: Full support for all Power BI service features.

questions.explanation: DirectQuery mode relies on the source system to run queries in real time, so performance depends on the data source's speed and responsiveness. Data is NOT cached (option C is false). Some Power BI features may be limited in DirectQuery (D is false). Scheduled refresh is not needed because the data is queried live, so A is false.

questions.question: In Dual storage mode, how does Power BI determine whether to use Import or DirectQuery for a particular query?

choices.A: The user manually chooses the mode per query.
choices.B: Power BI automatically decides the most efficient mode to retrieve data.
choices.C: It always uses Import mode unless data is missing.
choices.D: It always queries the live data source first, then falls back to Import mode.

questions.explanation: Dual mode allows Power BI to dynamically decide the best mode for data retrieval, optimizing performance and freshness. The user does not manually select the mode per query.

questions.question: What is the primary reason an organization might choose DirectQuery mode over Import mode?

choices.A: To take advantage of faster query performance.
choices.B: To ensure data is always up to date and avoid local data storage due to security concerns.
choices.C: To use all Power BI features without limitation.
choices.D: To reduce dependency on the data source’s availability.

questions.explanation: DirectQuery mode ensures real-time data access and avoids local storage, which can be critical for security reasons or regulatory compliance. Import mode stores a copy locally and requires refresh. Query performance is typically slower in DirectQuery (so A is false). Some features are limited in DirectQuery (C is false). DirectQuery increases dependency on source availability (D is false).

questions.question: Which Power BI feature is NOT fully supported when using DirectQuery mode?

choices.A: Q&A natural language queries
choices.B: Basic visualizations like bar charts
choices.C: Filters and slicers
choices.D: Real-time data updates

questions.explanation: Q&A and some AI-driven features (like Quick Insights) are limited or unavailable in DirectQuery mode because these features rely on imported data models. Basic visuals, filters, and real-time data work in DirectQuery.

questions.question: How can you change the storage mode of a table in Power BI Desktop?

choices.A: From the Data view by right-clicking the table.
choices.B: In the Model view by selecting the table and using the Properties pane.
choices.C: In the Report view by selecting the visual connected to the table.
choices.D: From the Power BI Service portal settings.

questions.explanation: Storage mode is set in the Model view of Power BI Desktop. You select the table, then adjust the mode via the Properties pane’s Storage Mode drop-down.

questions.question: If you want some tables imported for faster querying and others queried live due to size or security, which storage mode do you use?

choices.A: Import
choices.B: DirectQuery
choices.C: Dual
choices.D: Live Connection

questions.explanation: Dual mode (also called Composite mode) allows mixing Import and DirectQuery for different tables in the same model, optimizing performance and freshness.

questions.question: What happens if a table in Dual mode is queried for data that exists in both Import and DirectQuery cache?

choices.A: Power BI always uses the DirectQuery source.
choices.B: Power BI always uses the cached Import data.
choices.C: Power BI chooses the method that results in better performance.
choices.D: The query fails due to ambiguity.

questions.explanation: Power BI intelligently decides which mode to use (Import cache or DirectQuery) to maximize performance and efficiency.

questions.question: Why might an organization prohibit importing local copies of data into Power BI?

choices.A: To reduce file size of the Power BI report.
choices.B: Due to data security and compliance policies.
choices.C: Because Import mode is slower than DirectQuery.
choices.D: To avoid using Power BI features that require Import mode.

questions.explanation: Importing local copies can violate data governance or security policies, especially if data is sensitive or regulated. Reducing file size is secondary, and Import mode is usually faster (C is false). Avoiding Power BI features is unlikely to be a reason (D is false).

questions.question: What is a primary advantage of using the "Connect live" option when connecting Power BI to Azure Analysis Services?

choices.A: It allows you to import data faster than the Import option.
choices.B: It keeps DAX calculations and data refreshes centralized in Azure Analysis Services.
choices.C: It enables Power BI to write back data to the Azure Analysis Services model.
choices.D: It automatically converts MDX queries to T-SQL for better performance.

questions.explanation: "Connect live" keeps the data and DAX calculations within Azure Analysis Services, allowing centralized management and immediate refresh in reports without importing data into Power BI. Options A, C, and D are incorrect because import can be slower, Power BI cannot write back to AAS, and queries are not converted to T-SQL.

questions.question: Which of the following languages can you use to query data directly from Azure Analysis Services models?

choices.A: T-SQL
choices.B: MDX
choices.C: DAX
choices.D: Both B and C

questions.explanation: Azure Analysis Services models can be queried using MDX and DAX. T-SQL is used for SQL Server but not for AAS tabular models.

questions.question: In Azure Analysis Services, why might you prefer to import all additional data sources into the AAS model and then connect live from Power BI instead of importing multiple data sources directly into Power BI?

choices.A: To reduce the size of the Power BI report.
choices.B: To consolidate semantic modeling and DAX calculations in a single place.
choices.C: To avoid using DAX calculations altogether.
choices.D: To prevent Power BI from authenticating to multiple data sources.

questions.explanation: Consolidating data sources in AAS centralizes semantic modeling and DAX logic, simplifying maintenance and improving performance. Options A, C, and D are incorrect as import size reduction is a side effect, DAX is still used, and authentication still happens.

questions.question: What is a key difference between Azure Analysis Services and SQL Server when retrieving data for Power BI reports?

choices.A: Azure Analysis Services requires using T-SQL for queries.
choices.B: Azure Analysis Services provides pre-built calculations within the model.
choices.C: SQL Server can only be queried live, not imported.
choices.D: Power BI cannot authenticate to Azure Analysis Services servers.

questions.explanation: AAS models often contain pre-built calculations (measures) using DAX. SQL Server queries use T-SQL and lack this embedded semantic modeling. Other options are false.

questions.question: When connecting Power BI to Azure Analysis Services, which of the following is NOT true?

choices.A: You must provide the server address and database name.
choices.B: You can select specific tables from the model for use.
choices.C: You can write back data changes to the Azure Analysis Services model directly from Power BI.
choices.D: You can use either Import or Connect live as a connection option.

questions.explanation: Power BI only reads data from AAS; it cannot write back data or changes. Other statements are true.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the refresh behavior when using the “Connect live” option with Azure Analysis Services?

choices.A: Power BI schedules its own data refresh that happens independently from Azure Analysis Services.
choices.B: When data refreshes in Azure Analysis Services, Power BI reports reflect the changes immediately without a separate refresh.
choices.C: Connect live connections require manual refresh in Power BI every time data changes.
choices.D: The Connect live option disables data refresh capabilities entirely.

questions.explanation: With Connect live, Power BI queries data in real time from AAS. When AAS refreshes, reports immediately show updated data. Power BI does not require separate refresh for live connections.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of semantic models in Azure Analysis Services?

choices.A: To store raw transactional data from various sources.
choices.B: To provide a trusted, reusable layer combining data, calculations, and security for analytics.
choices.C: To replace Power BI datasets entirely.
choices.D: To enable data entry and manipulation via Excel spreadsheets.

questions.explanation: Semantic models unify data, calculations, and security, creating a trusted layer for analysis. They do not store raw transactional data primarily, nor replace Power BI datasets fully or allow data entry.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence when retrieving data from Azure Analysis Services to Power BI?

choices.A: Authenticate → Pick the model → Select tables → Write back data
choices.B: Authenticate → Select tables → Pick the model → Query data
choices.C: Authenticate → Pick the model → Select tables → Query data
choices.D: Select tables → Authenticate → Pick the model → Query data

questions.explanation: First authenticate, then choose the semantic model, select tables, then query data. Writing back is not supported.

questions.question: Why might you choose to query specific fields or measures instead of importing entire tables from Azure Analysis Services?

choices.A: To improve query performance and reduce data volume.
choices.B: Because Azure Analysis Services does not allow importing entire tables.
choices.C: To avoid using DAX calculations.
choices.D: Because Power BI does not support full table imports from AAS.

questions.explanation: Querying specific fields/measures reduces data volume and improves performance. AAS does allow importing full tables, and DAX is still used.

questions.question: How does Azure Analysis Services help secure data for enterprise use?

choices.A: By storing all data encrypted on-premises only.
choices.B: By providing a centralized, trusted semantic model with security roles applied.
choices.C: By automatically encrypting data inside Power BI reports.
choices.D: By restricting user access to only import mode in Power BI.

questions.explanation: AAS lets you define security roles and permissions on the semantic model, centralizing data access control. The other options are incorrect.

questions.question: What does a “fast refresh schedule” in Azure Analysis Services enable?

choices.A: Power BI reports update immediately when the AAS data refreshes without manual refresh in Power BI.
choices.B: Power BI data imports faster but with delay in report updates.
choices.C: Azure Analysis Services refreshes data only once per day.
choices.D: Users have to refresh Power BI manually after AAS refresh.

questions.explanation: Fast refresh means Power BI live reports reflect data immediately after AAS refreshes, no manual refresh needed.

questions.question: Why are Azure Analysis Services tabular models considered compatible with Power BI?

choices.A: Because both use the tabular model format and DAX for calculations.
choices.B: Because Power BI automatically converts tabular models to relational tables.
choices.C: Because both use T-SQL to query the data.
choices.D: Because tabular models only store data, no calculations.

questions.explanation: Both AAS and Power BI use the tabular model and DAX, making them fully compatible for live connections and shared calculations.

questions.question: In the given scenario, why would Tailwind Traders use Azure Analysis Services to store financial projections but keep actual sales data in a different database?

choices.A: To separate modeling and transactional systems for better performance and manageability.
choices.B: Because Azure Analysis Services cannot store sales data.
choices.C: To avoid using Power BI for sales data analysis.
choices.D: Because actual sales data cannot be connected to Power BI.

questions.explanation: Separating projection data (analytical) from transactional sales data allows optimized storage and processing for each. AAS is designed for analytics, not transactional storage.

questions.question: What advanced features does Azure Analysis Services provide to enhance data mashup and modeling?

choices.A: Predefined T-SQL queries for all data sources.
choices.B: Ability to combine data from multiple sources, define metrics, and create secure semantic models.
choices.C: Automatic generation of Power BI reports.
choices.D: Integration only with Excel and no other tools.

questions.explanation: AAS offers advanced mashup and modeling capabilities that let users combine data sources, define metrics, and secure the semantic model. It does not provide predefined T-SQL queries or automatic report generation.

questions.question: Which of the following transformations in Power Query cannot be folded into a native SQL query?

choices.A: Filtering rows with a WHERE clause
choices.B: Renaming columns
choices.C: Adding an index column
choices.D: Grouping rows using GROUP BY

questions.explanation: Adding an index column is a local transformation in Power Query that cannot be translated into a native SQL query, thus breaking query folding. Filtering, renaming columns, and grouping can be folded because they map directly to SQL operations.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of query folding in Power BI?

choices.A: It compresses data automatically in Power BI Desktop
choices.B: It runs transformations on the source server to reduce workload in Power BI
choices.C: It converts all Power BI visuals into SQL statements
choices.D: It optimizes memory usage within the Power BI service

questions.explanation: Query folding pushes data transformations to the source database, leveraging its processing power and reducing the workload on Power BI, which improves performance and refresh times.

questions.question: In which of the following scenarios would query folding not occur?

choices.A: Applying a filter to a column in a SQL Server table
choices.B: Renaming columns in a SQL Server query
choices.C: Merging two tables from two different data sources
choices.D: Grouping rows with aggregation functions on a SQL Server table

questions.explanation: Query folding requires that transformations be representable as a single SQL query on one data source. Merging tables from different sources breaks this requirement and disables folding.

questions.question: What tool can you use in Power Query Editor to identify which step in your query is causing performance issues?

choices.A: Performance Analyzer
choices.B: Query Diagnostics
choices.C: Query Folding Viewer
choices.D: Data Profiling

questions.explanation: Query Diagnostics in Power Query Editor helps monitor the execution time of each query step, identifying slow steps and bottlenecks during data transformations.

questions.question: Which practice helps improve performance when using DirectQuery mode in Power BI?

choices.A: Importing all data into Power BI before applying transformations
choices.B: Using native SQL queries instead of stored procedures or CTEs
choices.C: Applying all data transformations inside Power BI Desktop
choices.D: Combining date and time columns into a single column

questions.explanation: DirectQuery performance is better when native SQL queries are used, as stored procedures or CTEs can prevent query folding and reduce performance.

questions.question: How do you verify if query folding is occurring for a given step in Power Query?

choices.A: Right-click the step and select 'View Native Query' if available
choices.B: Check the query folding status in the Performance Analyzer tool
choices.C: Use the Data Profiling pane to view folding indicators
choices.D: Export the query to SQL Server Management Studio

questions.explanation: In Power Query Editor, right-clicking an applied step and selecting 'View Native Query' (if enabled) shows the SQL query generated by folding, confirming that folding is happening.

questions.question: Why is it recommended to separate date and time columns before importing into Power BI?

choices.A: To enable query folding for date/time operations
choices.B: To increase compression and improve performance
choices.C: Because Power BI cannot read combined datetime fields
choices.D: To ensure compatibility with DirectQuery mode

questions.explanation: Separating date and time columns helps VertiPaq compression algorithms work more efficiently, improving data compression and overall performance.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a limitation of query folding?

choices.A: Query folding works only with import mode, not DirectQuery
choices.B: It can only fold transformations that can be expressed as a single SELECT SQL statement
choices.C: Query folding automatically converts all Power BI queries into stored procedures
choices.D: It allows transformations to be executed only on the Power BI service

questions.explanation: Query folding is limited to transformations representable as single SQL SELECT statements with clauses like WHERE, GROUP BY, JOIN. Complex transformations break folding.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended way to improve Power BI query performance?

choices.A: Process as much data as possible in the source database
choices.B: Use query diagnostics to find bottlenecks in Power Query transformations
choices.C: Use complex stored procedures extensively with DirectQuery
choices.D: Separate date and time columns for better compression

questions.explanation: Complex stored procedures with DirectQuery can hinder query folding and degrade performance. It is better to use simple native SQL queries.

questions.question: What does the Performance Analyzer tool in Power BI do?

choices.A: It analyzes query folding in Power Query Editor
choices.B: It identifies which visuals or filters take the longest to render in reports
choices.C: It diagnoses SQL server performance issues
choices.D: It automatically fixes performance issues in Power BI reports

questions.explanation: Performance Analyzer measures the rendering time of report visuals and filters to help identify and troubleshoot performance bottlenecks at the report level.

questions.question: Which storage modes in Power BI automatically support query folding?

choices.A: Import mode only
choices.B: DirectQuery and Dual storage modes
choices.C: Live Connection mode only
choices.D: None of the above

questions.explanation: DirectQuery and Dual storage modes require and automatically support query folding because they rely on pushing transformations to the data source.

questions.question: Why is query folding beneficial in terms of Power BI’s resource usage?

choices.A: It reduces the amount of data loaded by compressing it in memory
choices.B: It offloads data transformations to the source server, reducing workload on Power BI’s local computing resources
choices.C: It converts visuals to server-side rendering, saving client CPU
choices.D: It caches queries indefinitely to avoid refreshes

questions.explanation: Query folding pushes transformations to the data source, thus reducing CPU and memory usage on the Power BI client or service.

questions.question: If the 'View Native Query' option is not available for the last applied step, what should you do?

choices.A: Disable query folding in Power Query settings
choices.B: Remove all steps and start over
choices.C: Work backward through the Applied Steps until you find a step where 'View Native Query' is available
choices.D: Restart Power BI Desktop

questions.explanation: If folding breaks at a certain step, you can identify where it stops by moving backward through Applied Steps to find the last step supporting query folding.

questions.question: Which of the following SQL clauses are typically supported by query folding?

choices.A: GROUP BY, JOIN, WHERE, UNION ALL
choices.B: TRUNCATE, DROP, ALTER
choices.C: EXECUTE, CALL, BEGIN TRANSACTION
choices.D: INSERT, DELETE, UPDATE

questions.explanation: Query folding supports SELECT statement clauses like GROUP BY, JOIN, WHERE, and UNION ALL, which correspond to Power Query transformations.

questions.question: How does query folding impact incremental refresh in Power BI?

choices.A: It slows down refresh because data has to be imported again
choices.B: It enables more efficient incremental refresh by pushing filters and transformations to the data source
choices.C: It has no impact on incremental refresh
choices.D: It disables incremental refresh functionality

questions.explanation: Query folding enables incremental refresh to run efficiently by filtering and processing data partitions at the source, reducing load and improving refresh speed.

questions.question: What is the best strategy to resolve a "Query Timeout Expired" error when importing data from a SQL Server into Power BI?

choices.A: Increase the timeout settings in Power BI options.
choices.B: Import all the data at once and filter it later in Power BI.
choices.C: Break down the query into smaller parts and merge them in Power Query.
choices.D: Use Excel to load the data instead of SQL Server.

questions.explanation: The 'Query Timeout Expired' error occurs because the query is too complex or returns too much data, exceeding the server’s timeout limit. Increasing timeout in Power BI is not always possible or recommended, and importing all data at once will likely cause the same issue. The best practice is to divide the data into smaller, more manageable queries and then merge or append these queries in Power Query, reducing the load on the relational database and avoiding timeouts.

questions.question: You encounter the error "We couldn't find any data formatted as a table" when importing from Excel. What must you do to fix this issue?

choices.A: Save the Excel file in CSV format.
choices.B: Convert the Excel range into a table using Ctrl + T.
choices.C: Rename the Excel worksheet to 'Table'.
choices.D: Manually enter the data into Power BI.

questions.explanation: Power BI expects data imported from Excel to be formatted as an official Excel table (not just a cell range). Using Ctrl + T formats the selected range as a table with headers, which Power BI can recognize and import properly. Saving as CSV or renaming the worksheet will not fix this specific issue.

questions.question: When Power BI shows the "Couldn't find file" error during data import, what is the most likely cause and how should you fix it?

choices.A: The file was deleted; you must restore it from backup.
choices.B: The file path changed; update the file location in Power Query source settings.
choices.C: Power BI cannot open large files; reduce the file size.
choices.D: Your computer is offline; connect to the internet.

questions.explanation: This error usually means that Power BI can no longer locate the source file because it was moved or renamed. To fix it, open Power Query, select the query, then edit the Source step to update the file path to the correct location.

questions.question: Why might columns appear blank after importing data from SQL Server, and how can this be prevented?

choices.A: Power BI does not support some SQL data types; convert columns to supported types in the query.
choices.B: The SQL Server is offline; restart the server.
choices.C: Power BI only loads data when all columns are numeric.
choices.D: The query results are too large; filter the results to fewer rows.

questions.explanation: Blank columns often result from Power BI failing to interpret data types correctly. Casting or converting columns explicitly to supported types (e.g., varchar) in the SQL query prevents this issue by ensuring compatible data formats are sent to Power BI.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why relational databases implement query timeouts that can affect Power BI data imports?

choices.A: To stop queries that try to access restricted data.
choices.B: To prevent a single query from monopolizing system resources, protecting overall performance.
choices.C: To disconnect users who are inactive for long periods.
choices.D: To enforce company-wide data privacy policies.

questions.explanation: Query timeouts limit execution time of queries to prevent any single user or query from using excessive resources, which could degrade performance for others. This mechanism ensures fair resource sharing among many concurrent users or applications accessing the same database.

questions.question: If you need to import a large dataset with many columns from SQL Server but face timeout errors, which approach is recommended?

choices.A: Import all columns in one query but increase timeout.
choices.B: Import half of the columns in one query and the rest in another, then merge in Power Query.
choices.C: Import only numeric columns to reduce processing time.
choices.D: Use direct query mode instead of import mode.

questions.explanation: Splitting columns into smaller queries and merging them in Power Query reduces query complexity and execution time. Increasing timeout may not be possible or advisable, and importing only numeric columns unnecessarily limits the dataset.

questions.question: You want to fix an error caused by changes in file permissions of a data source file. What steps should you take?

choices.A: Change the file permissions to allow Power BI access or contact your system administrator.
choices.B: Move the file to a different folder without changing permissions.
choices.C: Rename the file extension to .csv.
choices.D: Delete the file and recreate it.

questions.explanation: If permissions change and Power BI cannot access the file, you need to ensure Power BI has the necessary read permissions. This may require changing file/folder permissions or involving IT support.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended action when facing an unknown Power BI data import error?

choices.A: Searching Microsoft documentation for the error message.
choices.B: Breaking down the data import into smaller chunks using Power Query.
choices.C: Reformatting the entire data source from scratch without investigation.
choices.D: Checking and correcting data types at the data source or query level.

questions.explanation: Reformatting the entire data source without understanding the error is inefficient and unnecessary. Instead, research the error, optimize queries, and check data types.

questions.question: Which external factors outside of Power BI and data sources can cause data import errors?

choices.A: Network issues and slow internet connection.
choices.B: File permissions and hard drive errors.
choices.C: Operating system updates or failures.
choices.D: All of the above.

questions.explanation: Data import errors can arise from many external factors including network interruptions, file permissions, hardware issues, and OS-level problems affecting data accessibility during import.

questions.question: If you encounter a data import error not described in official Power BI documentation, what should be your best course of action?

choices.A: Ignore the error and retry the import repeatedly.
choices.B: Search for the exact error message on Microsoft documentation and community forums.
choices.C: Delete all queries and restart the Power BI project.
choices.D: Contact your database administrator without investigating.

questions.explanation: The best approach is to research the exact error message using official Microsoft docs and trusted community forums. This often provides specific resolutions or workarounds.
